Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.normDiscrete_associated_pow: The equality v(π) = 1 implies π is nonzero and v(πⁿ) = n. Since v(x) = n as well, the ratio x/πⁿ has valuation zero. It belongs to the valuation ring and is a unit there. Multiplying πⁿ by this unit gives x, proving that the elements are associated.
Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.normDiscrete_exists_nat: By discreteness the valuation of the nonzero element x is finite, so it is represented by an integer m. Membership in the valuation ring gives m ≥ 0. Take the natural number represented by m.
Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.normDiscrete_irreducible: An element of valuation 1 is not a unit, since units have valuation zero. If π = ab, the two factors have nonnegative valuations whose sum is 1. Neither valuation can be the top element, and the remaining values are nonnegative integers. One of the two values is therefore zero. The corresponding factor is a unit, proving irreducibility.
Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.normDiscrete_isDiscreteValuationRing: Choose π of valuation 1 using normalized discreteness. It lies in the valuation ring and is irreducible. Every nonzero element has a finite nonnegative integer valuation n and is associated to πⁿ. The criterion that a ring with such a uniformizer and factorization is a discrete valuation ring now applies.
Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.normDiscrete_isUnit_iff:
If x has an inverse y in the valuation ring, the valuations of x and y are nonnegative and sum to the valuation of 1, which is zero. Thus v(x) = 0.

Conversely, v(x) = 0 implies x ≠ 0 because the valuation of zero is the top element. The inverse has valuation −0 = 0 and belongs to the valuation ring. Together with the inverse identity in the field, this makes x a unit in the valuation ring.
Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.normDiscrete_map_inv: The valuation of an inverse is the negative of the valuation of the original element. Applying this identity and substituting v(x) = n gives v(x⁻¹) = −n.
Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.normDiscrete_mem_vRing_iff: By definition, the valuation ring consists of the elements with nonnegative valuation. Applying this definition to x gives the equivalence.

Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.finsum_fiberwise_of_finite_support:
Let S be the finite support of f. For each b, the sum of f on the fibre ρ⁻¹(b) is the finite sum over those a in S with ρ(a) = b. To see this, extend the summand on the fibre by zero to all of A. The extension is supported in S, and the terms outside the fibre vanish.

If b lies outside ρ(S), the fibre sum is zero. The outer sum can therefore be taken over the finite image ρ(S). The fibres over this image partition S, so adding their sums gives the sum of f over S, which is the original finitely supported sum.

Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.localization_away_injective_of_dvd:
Let I be the kernel of R → R_𝔭 and choose a finite generating set for I using Noetherianity. Each generator maps to zero in R_𝔭, so some element outside 𝔭 annihilates it. Take t to be the product of these elements, using 1 for the empty set. The complement of 𝔭 is multiplicatively closed, so t is outside 𝔭. It annihilates each generator and therefore all of I.

Write c = td and fix a compatible map κ from R[1/c] to R_𝔭. The images of t and d multiply to the unit image of c, so the image of t is a unit in R[1/c]. If a fraction a/cⁿ belongs to the kernel of κ, multiplying its image by the image of cⁿ shows that a maps to zero in R_𝔭. Hence a lies in I and ta = 0. Since t maps to a unit in R[1/c], a maps to zero there as well. The fraction is zero and κ is injective.

Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.X_pow_mul_C_mem_coneAlg: Let W be the range of ev. Induct on the construction of t as an element of Wᵈ. In degree zero, a ground scalar gives a constant polynomial, which lies in the algebra. Addition of elements of Wᵈ corresponds to addition of their degree-d monomials. In the multiplication step write the new coefficient as ev(v)t′, with t′ in the preceding power. Its monomial is the product of X·C(ev(v)) and the monomial for t′. The first factor is a generator of the cone algebra and the second belongs by induction.
Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.mem_coneAlg_iff_coeff:
Write W for the range of ev. For the forward direction, the condition that the coefficient of degree d belongs to Wᵈ is preserved by the operations generating the algebra. The generator X·C(ev(v)) has its only possibly nonzero coefficient in degree one, where it lies in W. Ground scalars contribute only in degree zero, where W⁰ is the ground-scalar submodule. The condition is closed under addition degree by degree. In a product, each contribution to degree d is a product of coefficients from degrees i and j with i+j=d, so it belongs to WⁱWʲ = Wᵈ. The sum of these contributions also belongs.

Conversely, expand p as the finite sum of its coefficient monomials. The preceding lemma puts each monomial Xᵈ·C(p_d) in the algebra because p_d belongs to Wᵈ. Closure under finite addition gives p in the cone algebra.

Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.coercive_of_re_pos:
Write q(x) = Re Q(x,x). If V has only the zero vector, q(0) = 0 by bilinearity and c = 1 suffices. Suppose V has a nonzero vector. Linear maps from a finite-dimensional normed space are continuous, so Q can be viewed as a continuous linear map into the space of continuous linear maps V → ℂ. Evaluating on the diagonal and taking the real part gives a continuous function q.

The unit sphere is nonempty and compact, so q has a minimum c there. Every unit vector is nonzero, hence the positivity hypothesis gives c > 0. For x ≠ 0, set u = x/‖x‖. Then u has norm one, and bilinearity gives q(x) = ‖x‖² q(u) ≥ ‖x‖² c. At x = 0 both sides vanish.

Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.GlobalTheory.Fc.of_hyps: Apply the shape theorem to the family and selections carried by the hypothesis record. Pass the S-component of each C-selection. Translate the divisibility rows and the service condition using their equivalences in the shape interface. For the rank rows, retain the existing constants and eventual threshold, and keep the listed fields of the first row together with the second row intact. This gives the row condition in the form required by the shape theorem. The record and the supplied proofs of V and NR give all remaining inputs, so the theorem yields G.
Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.GlobalTheory.Fc.shape_of: Fix the four parameters and the shape theorem. Apply of_hyps with the supplied proofs of V and NR and the family hypothesis record to obtain G.

Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.rootOfUnity_mem_range_Om: Choose a primitive mth root ζ in Om ℓ. The embedding into ℂ_[ℓ] is injective, so the image of ζ is still primitive of order m. Its m powers from exponent 0 through m−1 are distinct roots of X^m−1. Since that polynomial has degree m, these exhaust its roots. In particular x is one of those powers. The same power of ζ in Om ℓ maps to x because the embedding preserves powers.

Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.Val.pow:
Unpack the normal-form data for a value of x. Each entry of the two characteristic vectors is either zero or one half, so both vectors coincide pointwise with their real-part vectors viewed over ℂ. The power formula for normal forms then gives the transformed data for y and its determinant relation.

Use the transformed data as the witnesses for the value of y. The new constant is cʲ and is nonzero because c is nonzero. Substituting the determinant relation and combining the powers gives the value tʲ.
Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.exists_known_rat:
Start with the rational elliptic curve y² = x³ − x. Its elliptic key has genus one and known value equal to the discriminant. Take its gth key power to get genus g. The proposed known value is the gth power of the discriminant.

After extension to ℂ, choose normal-form data for the original elliptic key. The discriminant formula gives its value in this normal form. The key power raises that value to the gth power by the formula for values of key powers. The base-change comparison and cancellation identify this normal form with the one for the given complex key of genus g, giving the required known value.
Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/.isElliptic_cube_sub: Compute the Weierstrass invariants of the model y² = x³ − x and substitute them in the discriminant formula. The discriminant is 64. It is nonzero, hence a unit in ℚ, which is the ellipticity criterion for the model.

Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.factor_ne_zero: The prime p exceeds 1, and Re(s) is positive, so the norm of p^(−s) is p^(−Re(s)) < 1. The norm of the character value is at most 1, hence the norm of their product is strictly below 1. The product cannot equal 1, which proves the Euler factor is nonzero.
Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.gamma_ne_zero: Distinguish even and odd characters. Their gamma factors are Γℝ(s) and Γℝ(s + 1), respectively. Positive real part of s implies positive real part of both arguments, so the factors are nonzero.
Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.prim_reflect: The gamma factor is nonzero at s, so the zero of the ordinary L-function gives a zero of the completed L-function. The inverse character is primitive by invariance of the conductor under inversion. Its functional equation transfers the completed zero to 1 − s. Since 1 − s is distinct from zero, the expression for the ordinary L-function in terms of the completed one gives the desired zero.
Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.prim_zero: The change-of-level formula expresses the original L-value as the primitive L-value times a product of Euler factors. Here s is distinct from 1 because Re(s) < 1. Each Euler factor is nonzero since Re(s) > 0 makes the term subtracted from 1 have absolute value less than 1. The product can therefore vanish only through the primitive L-value.
Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.strip: A zero above the critical line in real part contradicts right half-plane nonvanishing. For a zero below the critical line, first pass to the primitive character using the change-of-level formula. Its functional equation gives a zero at 1 − s for the inverse character. The reflected point has real part greater than 1/2 and is distinct from 1 because Re(s) > 0. This contradicts the same nonvanishing hypothesis, leaving Re(s) = 1/2.
Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.zeta:
A zero with real part at least 1 contradicts the usual zeta nonvanishing theorem. When the real part lies strictly between 0 and 1, view zeta as the L-function of the character of modulus 1 and apply the Dirichlet critical-strip result.

It remains to consider Re(s) ≤ 0. The value at zero is nonzero. The exclusions on s also ensure Γℝ(s) is nonzero, since its other zeros are the negative even integers. Thus the completed zeta function vanishes at s. Its functional equation transfers the zero to 1 − s, where the ordinary zeta function would then vanish with real part at least 1. This is impossible.
Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.zeta_iff: Both statements say that every zero of the zeta function other than 1 and the negative even integers has real part 1/2. Each direction follows by using the same hypothesis on those zeros.

Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.topDesWin:
Combine the nine closed link conditions into one. Let ε₁ be its positive cutoff and ε₃ the positive cutoff for design existence. For 0 < ε < min(ε₁, ε₃), choose the threshold K given by the combined closed condition. Design existence above K produces a family in 𝒞′, together with its chosen data and size bounds. Map its class membership to 𝒞 to apply the closed conditions and to ℰ for the conclusion.

The ℰ membership gives the eventual volume bound. Use it with the N-link and the small-level rank equality to obtain divisibility in N. The closed divisibility condition, together with the eta and size inputs, then gives the required divisibility link. Combine this with the rank conditions and the two size estimates to obtain the μ-link. The global link now applies to the G, S, irreducibility, divisibility, and μ-links, producing the tied family required for connectedness.

Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.UpperTheory.Top.plugAll: First apply the preceding theorem to obtain the zero-free statement for primitive characters. Apply the imprimitive reduction to extend that statement to every Dirichlet character.
Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.UpperTheory.Top.plugWin: Take a witness of the family hypotheses. The Green condition supplies the shape theorem for these families, and applying it to the witness gives the connectedness criterion for the required families. For each primitive character ψ, the window input at ψ gives the required host existence by the host existence theorem for a character window. Apply the primitive-character nonvanishing theorem with these two inputs and window parameter 3/2, which exceeds 1.

Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.UpperTheory.Top.hostOfField: Apply the host construction from field data. It takes the uniform short-norm estimates, including the estimate with norm bound one. With those inputs fixed, the construction supplies the constants and, for each admissible field datum in range, a host together with the required sharing estimate.
Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.UpperTheory.Top.supplyOfAdm: The general supply theorem converts admissible rank data and a character window into host existence. Use the preceding field-to-host construction. The resulting hosts satisfy both the cyclic-level estimate and the volume bound at the square root of the scale parameter.

Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.UpperTheory.Top.imprimitive:
Let ψ be the primitive character inducing χ. Primitive nonvanishing gives L(ψ,s) ≠ 0. If χ is nonprincipal, then ψ is nonprincipal, since changing the level of a principal character still gives a principal character. If s ≠ 1 this condition on the character is unnecessary. Thus the hypotheses allow the change-of-level formula for L(χ,s).

That formula multiplies L(ψ,s) by factors 1 − ψ(p)p^(−s). For each prime p in the product, |ψ(p)| ≤ 1 and |p^(−s)| = p^(−Re(s)) < 1, since p > 1 and Re(s) > 1/2. Hence ψ(p)p^(−s) cannot be 1. All factors in the formula are nonzero, so L(χ,s) is nonzero.

Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter: The integral Galois compatibility theorem applied to the local reciprocity parameter gives the compatibility hypothesis of the preceding nonvanishing result. That result applies to every character.

Use the Galois compatibility hypothesis to supply both compatibility entries of the literature hypotheses. The local reciprocity existence theorem supplies the remaining entry. The same Galois compatibility hypothesis gives the required window estimate. Apply the nonvanishing theorem with these literature hypotheses and that estimate.
Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.riemannHypothe: The preceding theorem supplies nonvanishing to the right of the critical line for all Dirichlet characters. The reduction from this nonvanishing statement gives the Riemann Hypothesis.

Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.UpperTheory.riemannHypothesis_of_everyCh:
Let s be a nontrivial zero of the zeta function, with s ≠ 1. The right half-plane nonvanishing just proved rules out Re(s) > 1/2. Suppose Re(s) < 1/2. The value ζ(0) = −1/2 gives s ≠ 0. Then 1 − s is distinct from both 0 and 1, and Re(1 − s) > 1/2.

Write ζ(s) as the completed zeta function divided by Γℝ(s). A zero of Γℝ occurs only at 0 or a negative even integer, and both possibilities are excluded here. Hence the completed zeta function vanishes at s. Its functional equation gives the same zero at 1 − s. The quotient formula there gives ζ(1 − s) = 0, contradicting right half-plane nonvanishing. Thus Re(s) = 1/2.
Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.UpperTheory.zeta_ne_zero_of_everyCharact: Take the unique character modulo 1. Its L-function is the Riemann zeta function. Apply the assumed nonvanishing to this character and the given point s. The hypothesis s ≠ 1 supplies the required disjunction even for the principal character.

Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.UpperTheory.Top.shapeWin:
Build the closed conditions for the design theorem from the given selections. The real-place tie, mass ratio, and genus mass inputs give the chosen-rank condition and the global link by the global-link theorem. To obtain the divisibility condition, first collect the restriction rows, stable cuts, chosen rows, one-map condition, nonnegative size, admissible twist link, and the two selection conditions. These conditions hold together by closure. For a family satisfying them, the wiring selection supplies the row maps when the required N-link is available. Use these maps and the collected conditions to form the bridge rows, then use the closed divisibility-link theorem.

For the existence input, intersect the original family class with the requested G-class. Restrict the selection and duty to this intersection. Forgetting the G-condition gives the original twisted and smoothed families, so the closed size and level conditions restrict as well. The design existence theorem now supplies designs in the intersection. Apply the design-window theorem with those designs, the closed divisibility condition just proved, and the eta, irreducibility, rank, G, S, and global links. The resulting connectedness is that of the requested G-class.

Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.at_of_from: The From relation identifies the ranks of the point with R and identifies the transported host data with those of H. It also identifies the images of the two sets TT in the ambient frame coordinates. The frame coordinate map is injective, so equality of images gives equality of the sets themselves. After these identifications, the defining arguments of G.At at the point are exactly the arguments in the hypothesis on G.

Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.UpperTheory.Top.supplyChi: Fix ψ and its window input. The admissible-host supply theorem reduces the conclusion to producing an admitted rank datum for each sufficiently large scale with the specified order and character-kernel conditions. For each ε in the required range, choose the threshold from the twisted-character admissibility theorem. After identifying the scale parameter with ε, the scale, order, and host assumptions are exactly those used by that theorem. Its rank datum supplies the admissible rank data required for host existence.

Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.eFamC_of_cls: Use the constant 4 and the eventual threshold x₁ + 1. The character-family hypothesis supplies the cyclic-level estimate at the chosen host. Its scale coordinates are x and ε, by the two scale identities for the family. Substituting these coordinates gives the asserted eventual condition.
Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.hypV_of_cls: Take the eventual threshold x₁ + 1. At each x beyond this threshold and each index i, membership in the character family gives the two bounds at the corresponding host. The second is the required eventual volume bound.
Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Charac.zeroFreeAll_of_topG: Use the cyclic tied-window nonvanishing theorem with the given scaled families and their chain relation. Its comparison hypotheses are the level bound on family scales and the form-B theorem. For each ψ, apply the connectedness criterion using the host existence and eventual volume bound for the family class of ψ. This gives the exponents, a positive ε cutoff, and the required families. Each family supplies the eventual cyclic-level estimate by the preceding lemma, its windows directly from class membership, and the tie data from connectedness. The resulting nonvanishing theorem applies to every primitive character.

Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/ThetaC.UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.every_cha: Obtain the eigenvalue and first-stage results from the literature interface O. The same interface yields agreement of the theta integrals and local matching. Use the geometric and arithmetic results in O, together with the Hilbert–Samuel and bigness estimates, to obtain the covolume estimate. Supply these inputs, the local reciprocity existence theorem, and the window hypothesis to the nonvanishing result based on theta-integral agreement and local matching.

Development/AutomorphicSpectrum/Proofs/B.comparison_degree_one_bijective: A degree-one cochain is indexed by pairs of objects T, T′ and arrows T → T′. On the component for an arrow the semilinear comparison acts by the component map at T′. Its lift is bijective by the objectwise bijectivity lemma. Apply the finite-product lemma to the arrows for each fixed pair, then to T′ for each T, and finally to T.
Development/AutomorphicSpectrum/Proofs/B.comparison_degree_two_bijective: A degree-two cochain is indexed by triples of objects T, T′, T″ and composable arrows T → T′ → T″. The component map is the map at the final object T″, whose lift is bijective. Combine these lifts with the finite-product lemma, first over the second arrow, then over the first arrow, and then over T″, T′, and T in that order.
Development/AutomorphicSpectrum/Proofs/B.comparison_degree_zero_bijective: A degree-zero cochain has one component for each object T. The comparison map is the lift of the product of the component maps at these objects. Each objectwise lift is bijective by the objectwise bijectivity lemma. Apply the finite-product lemma to the object index.
Development/AutomorphicSpectrum/Proofs/B.liftSemi_cT_bijective: The base-change data at T provides an S-linear equivalence e sending 1 ⊗ b to the image of b under the component map at T. By S-linearity e sends s ⊗ b to s times that image. This is also the value of the objectwise lift on s ⊗ b by the pure tensor formula. The lifts agree on pure tensors and extend additively, so the objectwise lift equals e and is bijective.
Development/AutomorphicSpectrum/Proofs/B.liftSemi_piS_bijective: For the finite index set I, tensoring with S over R identifies the tensor product of S with ∏ᵢ Mᵢ with the product ∏ᵢ (S ⊗ Mᵢ). Under this identification the lifted product map is the product of the individual lifted maps. Indeed, on a pure tensor s ⊗ x its i-th component is s · uᵢ(xᵢ) on both sides. The maps are additive, so the identity holds on all tensors. Each component lift is bijective by hypothesis, and their product composed with the tensor-product identification is bijective.
Development/AutomorphicSpectrum/Proofs/B.th_bijective: The opposite of the finite poset P has finitely many objects. Each hom-set in its category has at most one element because an arrow is specified by a single order relation. The degree-zero, degree-one, and degree-two comparison lemmas now apply to the given base-change data. Together they prove the three bijectivity assertions.

Development/AutomorphicSpectrum/Proofs/B.liftSemi_tmul: Through the algebra map R → S, the target is an R-module and the semilinear map f becomes R-linear. The base-change lift extends this map to the tensor product. The extension is S-linear and sends 1 ⊗ x to f(x), so it sends s ⊗ x = s · (1 ⊗ x) to s · f(x).

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordVectorInl_inl: The first coordinate vector is formed by retaining the pullback coordinates on the first index block and putting zero on the second. A first-block index selects the original pullback section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordVectorInl_inr: At a second-block index, the first coordinate vector takes the prescribed zero value.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordVectorInr_inl: The second coordinate vector has zero in every first-block position, so it is zero at the given index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordVectorInr_inr: On the second index block, the second coordinate vector retains the pullback sections. Its value at b is the pullback of the b-th coordinate along f.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_def: The coordinate section associated to f is defined by pulling the indicated affine-space coordinate back to a global section on Y.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineOpenIsoSpec_hom_appTop_apply: The affine identification uses first the spectrum of the global sections of the open subscheme and then the isomorphism of that ring with the section ring on W′. Naturality for spectrum maps transfers a through the inverse section-ring identification. The affine comparison then pulls that section back unchanged to the open subscheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceOpenIsoSpecMvPolynomial_hom_a: The constant polynomial a is the pullback of the base section a under the spectrum map of the coefficient inclusion. That map corresponds to the projection from relative affine space to its base. Transport to W′ using the affine identification. Compatibility of the projection with this transport gives the pullback of the section on the open subscheme corresponding to a.

Over the spectrum of the section ring on W′, the identification of affine space with the spectrum of a polynomial ring sends the variable section to the corresponding affine coordinate. Pulling back along the affine-space map induced by the identification of W′ with that spectrum preserves each coordinate. This gives the claimed coordinate on affine space over W′.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraEtale_comp_equiv: Transport the target of the étale algebra map along the target isomorphism. The transported algebra remains étale over R. The source isomorphism is itself étale, so composing with it gives an étale algebra over R′.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraEtale_congr: The two ring maps coincide, so they induce the same algebra structure. The étaleness condition on that structure transfers directly.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraEtale_of_ringHomEtale: An étale ring map is one whose associated algebra structure is étale. The hypothesis gives precisely that property for the algebra induced by f.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartAlgebra_etale:
Identify the relative affine space over W with the spectrum of the polynomial ring over the sections on W. The chart map followed by this isomorphism is étale between affine schemes, so its map on global sections is étale. Transport this map to the polynomial ring and the ring of sections on V by their canonical isomorphisms.

To identify the transported map with chart evaluation, compare the polynomial generators. A constant is pulled back along the projection to W and then along the chart, which is the coefficient map. A variable is pulled back as the corresponding affine coordinate section, which is the variable value in evaluation. Both maps therefore agree on all polynomials, proving étaleness of the chart algebra.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartAlgebra_formallyEtale: The chart algebra is étale by the preceding result, and every étale algebra is formally étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartAlgebra_isScalarTower: The polynomial algebra on V is induced by evaluation. A section on W enters the polynomial ring as a constant. Evaluating it yields its pullback along h by the constant formula, which is the direct action of the base section ring on V. The agreement gives the scalar tower.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartEvalHom_C: Evaluate the equality between the coefficient map of polynomial evaluation and the section pullback at the scalar section a.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartEvalHom_comp_C: The polynomial evaluation acts on constants by the coefficient map. That coefficient map pulls sections back along the chart followed by the projection. The hypothesis identifies that composite with the restriction of h, and the section-ring identifications therefore make it the section pullback along h. Thus the two ring maps agree on every coefficient.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_appTop_apply: The operation of pulling back global sections is contravariant. Pullback along the composite first pulls back z along the second map and then along the first.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isoSpec_hom_appTop_apply: The canonical map from the affine scheme Z to the spectrum of its global section ring induces the canonical identification of global sections with that ring. A section corresponding to a on the spectrum therefore pulls back to a on Z.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.resLE_appTop_conj_topIso_eq_appLE: Substitute the formula for the pullback on global sections of the open subschemes. On each end the identification and its inverse cancel, leaving the section pullback from W′ to V′.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.resLE_appTop_eq: Identify global sections of each open subscheme with sections over the corresponding open of the ambient scheme. Under these identifications, pulling back global sections along the restricted map is the section pullback from W′ to V′. This gives the stated composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specMap_appTop_apply: Under the canonical identifications of a ring with the global sections of its spectrum, pulling back along the spectrum map of u is the ring map u. Applying this identification to a gives the displayed section.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.algebraMap_eq_coordRingHom: The chart algebra structure is the one induced by the coordinate-ring map, so its structure map is that ring map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.algebra_etale: The structure map of the chart algebra is the étale coordinate-ring map. This is precisely étaleness of the algebra.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.algebra_formallyEtale: By the preceding result the chart algebra is étale. Formal étaleness is one of the conditions of étaleness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.coordRingHom_C: Evaluate the formula for the composite with the constant inclusion at a. The result is its scalar section on U.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.coordRingHom_X: The global section of affine space corresponding to the j-th polynomial variable is the j-th affine coordinate. The chart ring map pulls this section back to U, which is the definition of the j-th chart coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.coordRingHom_comp_C: On the polynomial spectrum the inclusion of constants corresponds to the projection to the spectrum of k. Transport that projection through the affine-space identification. By the defining commutative square of the chart, its composite with the chart is the structure map of the open subscheme U. Pullback on global sections and the identification with sections over U therefore give the scalar map induced by p.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.coordRingHom_def: The coordinate-ring map is defined by identifying polynomials with global sections of affine space, pulling those sections back along the chart, and identifying the resulting global sections with sections over U.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.coordRingHom_etale: Both the affine chart domain and the affine space over k are affine. Hence the étale chart induces an étale map on their global section rings. The coordinate-ring map is this map transported through the canonical identifications of the two rings. Because those identifications are isomorphisms, the coordinate-ring map is étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.coord_def: The chart coordinate is defined by pulling the affine coordinate back to a global section of the chart domain, then identifying it with a section over U in X.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.etaleCoordinates_coord: In the chart algebra, the coordinate is the image of its polynomial variable under the coordinate-ring map. The variable formula identifies that image with the geometric chart coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.ideal_eq_span_coord:
On the affine scheme U, the global ideal of the restricted ideal sheaf is the extension of the original section ideal on U along the canonical section-ring isomorphism. The global ideal of the chart ideal is generated by the affine coordinate sections indexed by S pulled back along the chart. Under the same section-ring isomorphism these generators correspond to the chart coordinates viewed as sections over U.

The restriction hypothesis identifies the two global ideals on the open subscheme. Extend back along the inverse section-ring isomorphism. The original section ideal is therefore generated by the chart coordinates indexed by S.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.isScalarTower: The scalar action through the polynomial ring sends a scalar to a constant polynomial and then applies the chart ring map. The constant formula identifies its value with the direct scalar section given by p. Agreement of the two scalar maps gives the tower.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceGlobalSectionsHom_X: Under pullback from affine space to the polynomial spectrum, the j-th coordinate becomes the section of the j-th variable. The map from polynomials to sections on affine space applies the inverse of that pullback. It therefore sends the variable back to the coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpace_specIso_hom_comp_specMap_C: The canonical identification of affine space with the polynomial spectrum is over the spectrum of K. The projection of the polynomial spectrum is induced by the inclusion of constants, so composing the identification with that projection gives the affine-space structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpace_specIso_inv_appTop_coord: The standard isomorphism from the spectrum of the coordinate polynomial ring to affine space pulls the j-th affine coordinate back to the global section corresponding to the j-th polynomial variable.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_top_comp_topIso_inv: Use the preceding description of the direct section pullback as global pullback followed by the section-ring identification on V. Composing with the inverse identification cancels it and leaves the global pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_comp_topIso_hom: Pullback of a global section along the inclusion of V followed by f is pullback by f followed by restriction to V. Identifying the result on the open subscheme V with a section on V gives the direct section map. The two restriction composites agree by functoriality of the presheaf.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_hom_appTop_inv_apply: The pullbacks on global sections induced by an isomorphism and its inverse are inverse ring maps, since pullback takes the composite identity to the identity. Applying the two pullbacks in succession returns x.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_presheafMap_comp_presheafMap: Compose the two restriction maps by functoriality of the presheaf. They are induced by the composite arrow, which equals the direct arrow because the category of opens has at most one arrow between any two objects. Precomposing with h gives the asserted equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_map_topIso_inv_injective: Apply ideal extension along the inverse isomorphism to both equal ideals in the global section ring of V. Each double extension is extension by the identity and therefore returns its original ideal. This gives equality of the original ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ι_appLE_top_eq_topIso_inv: The section map of the inclusion identifies a section over V with the same section viewed globally on the open subscheme V. This is the inverse of the identification in the other direction.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPrime_span_singleton_algebraMap_etaleC: The localization A is regular local by the étale localization theorem. The chosen coordinate lies in q, so its localized image lies in the maximal ideal of A. For this singleton set of coordinates, the étale cotangent-space result says that the class of the image is linearly independent in the cotangent space. The regular local ring criterion for an element with independent cotangent class gives that the ideal generated by the localized coordinate is prime.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_coordPolynomialRing_injective: The coordinate polynomial ring is a domain and the étale target is flat over it. A nonzero element of this domain acts injectively on the target by flatness. If such an element mapped to zero, it would act by the same value on 1 and 0, contradicting that the target ring is nonzero. The kernel of the structure map is therefore zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etaleChartCoord_injective: The coordinate polynomial ring maps injectively to the nonzero étale algebra by the preceding result. Distinct coordinate indices give distinct polynomial variables, so their images remain distinct.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRadical_map_span_singleton_prod_etaleC: Among the indices in T, let J consist of those whose coordinates lie in q. Every other coordinate maps to a unit in the localization. Thus the extension of the given product ideal has the same generator up to a unit as the product over J alone. That product ideal is radical by the localized result for coordinates lying in q.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRadical_span_singleton_of_isRadical_ma: Suppose a power of x belongs to the principal ideal I generated by a, and suppose x is outside I. The set of b such that bx belongs to I is an ideal, proper because 1 does not belong to it. Put this ideal inside a maximal ideal Q. In the localization at Q, the image of x has a power in the extended ideal and therefore belongs to that ideal by radicality. Membership in the localized ideal gives some element outside Q whose product with x lies in I, by clearing the localization denominators. This element would lie in the proper ideal chosen inside Q, a contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRadical_span_singleton_prod_algebraMap: The localization is regular local. Each selected coordinate lies in its maximal ideal because the original section lies in q. Their classes in the cotangent space are linearly independent by the preceding result. In a regular local ring the product of elements with independent cotangent classes generates a radical ideal. Apply that result to the finite family of selected coordinates.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRadical_span_singleton_prod_etaleChart: At every prime, the localized product ideal is radical by the preceding result. Apply the local criterion for radicality of a principal ideal to conclude that the original ideal is radical.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.linearIndependent_toCotangent_etaleChart:
The localized ring is regular local. Extend the selected coordinate sections to a regular system of parameters using the parameter extension theorem. Their localized images generate the maximal ideal, so the images of the parameters span the cotangent space after reducing the coefficients modulo the maximal ideal. The number of parameters is the Krull dimension, which equals the dimension of the cotangent space for a regular local ring. The spanning family is therefore linearly independent.

Each selected coordinate is represented by one of these parameter sections. The coordinate ring is nonzero because it maps to the local ring, so its distinct chart coordinates are distinct sections. Consequently the choice of a parameter index for each selected coordinate is injective. The corresponding subset of the cotangent basis is linearly independent, as required.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.X_pow_dvd_of_X_pow_dvd_X_mul: Induct on the exponent n. Divisibility by the zeroth power is automatic. For the successor step, divisibility of the product by the higher power implies divisibility by the j-th variable. The distinct-variable result then shows that this variable divides r. Write r as that variable times a polynomial. Cancel one copy of the nonzero variable in the domain. The induction hypothesis says the remaining polynomial is divisible by the n-th power, which recovers the required higher power in r.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_flat: Because r is a non-zero-divisor, multiplication by r is injective on R. Tensoring that injection with the flat R-algebra A gives an injective multiplication map on A. This map is multiplication by the image of r. By commutativity the image is a non-zero-divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_ι_top_eq_topIso_inv: The inclusion of V identifies a section on V with a global section of the open subscheme V. The map on sections is the inverse of the canonical identification from global sections back to sections on V.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.bijective_appLE_ι_top: The indicated section map is the inverse of the canonical ring isomorphism. It is therefore bijective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coord_mem_nonZeroDivisors: The relevant polynomial variable is nonzero in the polynomial ring over the field, which is a domain. It is therefore a non-zero-divisor. The chart algebra is étale and hence flat, so its image remains a non-zero-divisor. That image is the chart coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_mk_X_mul_eq_quotient_span_X: Choose polynomial representatives of a and b. The equality of the products says that the s-th variable times the difference of the representatives lies in the principal ideal of the j-th variable. The preceding divisibility result puts the difference itself in that ideal. Hence the two quotient classes agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_mk_X_mul_eq_quotient_span_X_pow: Choose representatives in the polynomial ring. The product equality means the s-th variable times their difference is divisible by the n-th power of the j-th variable. The power divisibility result shows that the difference itself is divisible by this power, so the classes coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_top_of_restrictIdeal_eq_top: The ideal of the restricted sheaf on the affine scheme V is the extension of the original section ideal along the canonical section-ring isomorphism. By hypothesis the extension is the whole ring. Contracting it back along the isomorphism gives the whole original ring, which is the asserted section ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor_of_lo: At x, choose the chart supplied by the hypothesis and shrink it to an affine neighbourhood. If D restricts to the unit ideal, its section ideal is generated by 1. Otherwise the restricted chart identifies its section ideal with the principal ideal of the chosen coordinate. That coordinate is a non-zero-divisor. In both cases this gives the required affine neighbourhood and generator.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_of_locally_coordIdeal: The local chart descriptions give a non-zero-divisor generator at each point by the preceding criterion. At a point of the support, the unit-ideal alternative cannot occur because the unit ideal has empty support on the chart. Thus at such a point the ideal is a coordinate hyperplane ideal. The smoothness result for closed subschemes that are locally coordinate subspaces applies, proving the second condition for a smooth divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_map_of_mul_mem_of_etale: Form the quotient of A by the extension of I. The induced map from the quotient of P is a base change of f, so it is étale and in particular flat. Multiplication by the class of w is injective on the source quotient by hypothesis and stays injective after this flat base change. The given product is zero in the target quotient, so the class of x is zero there. This is membership in the extended ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_span_X_of_X_mul_mem: Evaluate polynomials by setting the j-th variable to zero. The product of the s-th variable with r then evaluates to zero because it was a multiple of the j-th variable. The s-th variable is fixed by the evaluation and is nonzero in the polynomial domain. Thus r evaluates to zero. Passing to the quotient by the j-th variable is unchanged by the evaluation, as can be checked on constants and variables. It follows that r is zero in that quotient, so it belongs to the principal ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_span_coord_of_coord_mul_mem: Extension along the chart map sends the ideal of the j-th variable to the ideal of the j-th coordinate and sends the s-th variable to the s-th coordinate. Multiplication by the s-th variable is injective in the polynomial quotient by the j-th variable because the indices differ. Apply the étale quotient argument to transfer this injectivity to the chart quotient. The product hypothesis now gives that the class of x in the chart quotient is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_span_coord_pow_of_mul_mem: The ideal of the variable power extends to the ideal of the same power of the chart coordinate. The polynomial quotient by that power has injective multiplication by the s-th variable by the preceding result for distinct indices. The étale map on the quotients is flat, so multiplication by the s-th chart coordinate is also injective on the chart quotient. The product hypothesis therefore forces x to vanish in that quotient.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.notMem_support_of_mem_of_restrictIdeal_e: The support of the restriction is the inverse image of the original support. By hypothesis the restriction is the unit ideal, which has empty support. Therefore x, a point of U, is outside the original support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_eq_restrict_coordIdeal_of_: Restriction of Z to V is obtained by pulling its restriction to U back along the inclusion of V in U. On U that ideal is itself the pullback of the coordinate subspace ideal along the chart. Thus the restriction to V is the pullback along the composite defining the restricted chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_eq_top_of_le: Pull back the restriction of Z on U along the inclusion of V. By hypothesis it is the unit ideal, and pullback of the unit ideal is again the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_of_iSup_eq_top: The supremum condition means that the opens cover the source. Smoothness is local on the source in the Zariski topology. Since the restriction to each member of this cover is smooth, the map is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_subschemeι_comp_of_hasStrictNorma: At each point of the support, the strict normal crossing hypothesis provides a chart in which Z is a coordinate subspace. This is exactly the hypothesis of the local smoothness criterion for the closed subscheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_subschemeι_comp_of_locally_eq_coo: Each point of the closed subscheme maps into the support of Z. At its image choose the neighbourhood and chart supplied by the hypothesis. Shrink the neighbourhood to an affine open containing that image. The equality of ideals persists for the restricted chart. The preceding chart result gives smoothness on the inverse image of this affine open in the closed subscheme. These inverse images cover the subscheme, so smoothness holds globally by locality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_ι_comp_subschemeι_comp_of_eq_coor: The chart restricts to an étale chart on the part of the closed subscheme over U. Setting the coordinates indexed by S to zero reduces the target to affine space of dimension m minus the number of those coordinates. The structure map of the closed subscheme on this open is the composite of that étale map with the smooth affine-space projection. Both maps are smooth, so the composite is smooth.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etaleChartCoord_def: The j-th chart coordinate is the image in S of the polynomial variable indexed by j. This is exactly the formula defining the coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_and_ringKrullDim_eq_o:
Let p be the contraction of q to P. Every element outside p maps outside q and hence to a unit in A. The map from P to A therefore factors through the local ring at p. This factor is local. If a fraction from that local ring maps to a unit in A, its numerator also maps to a unit because its denominator does. The numerator then lies outside p, so the fraction was already a unit at p.

Étaleness of P → S and localization at q give flatness, formal unramifiedness, and essential finite type for the map from P to A. These properties give the corresponding properties for the factored map from the local ring at p. The local rings are Noetherian because P is Noetherian and S is of finite type over it. The local ring at p is regular by hypothesis. The regularity and dimension theorem for flat, formally unramified maps of these local rings now gives regularity of A and equality of its dimension with the dimension at p.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_localization_atPrime_: The prime localization of S at q is a localization at the complement of q. Take it as A in the preceding regularity result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_localization_coordPol: A polynomial ring in finitely many variables over a field is regular. Its localization at the prime p is a regular local ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_of_isLocalization_eta: The coordinate polynomial ring is Noetherian, and its prime localizations are regular local rings. Apply the preceding étale localization result with this ring as the base and take its regularity conclusion for A.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_etaleChartCoord_notMem_maxima:
Extend the partial derivation in the j-th coordinate from the chart algebra to its localization A. It takes the j-th coordinate to 1 and every coordinate indexed by J′ to zero. It sends the square of the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal, because the product rule for two elements in the maximal ideal leaves a factor from that ideal in each term.

It also sends the ideal generated by the selected coordinates into the maximal ideal. On a multiple of a selected coordinate, the derivative of the coordinate vanishes and the remaining term is divisible by the coordinate, which belongs to the maximal ideal. Additivity gives this for the entire ideal. If the j-th coordinate belonged to the sum of these ideals, its derivative 1 would lie in the maximal ideal, which is impossible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etaleChartCoordIdeal_eq_span_image: The chart coordinate ideal of J is defined to be generated by the images in S of the variables indexed by J.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etaleChartCoordIdeal_le: Each generator of the chart coordinate ideal lies in I by hypothesis. An ideal containing the generators contains their span.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_algebraMap_coordPolynomialRing: The structure map induces the given algebra structure on S because the two structures have the same scalar map. Étaleness of that algebra is precisely étaleness of its structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_regularSystemOfParameters_contain:
Let I be the ideal in A generated by the selected coordinates. The quotient by I is regular local. Choose generators of its maximal ideal in number equal to its dimension. Lift them to the maximal ideal of A, then write each lift as a fraction with numerator in S and denominator outside q. The numerator belongs to q because it is a unit multiple of an element of the maximal ideal after localization.

Use the selected coordinate sections and these numerators as the parameter list. All entries lie in q. The images of the numerators generate the maximal ideal modulo I because the denominators are units, and the selected coordinates generate I. Hence the localized list generates the maximal ideal of A. Its length is the dimension of the quotient plus the number of selected coordinates, which equals the dimension of A by the dimension formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_span_eq_maximalIdeal_card_eq_ring: Choose a basis of the cotangent space over the residue field and lift each basis vector to the maximal ideal. The residue field is a quotient of the local ring, so the lifted vectors generate the cotangent quotient as a module over the local ring. Nakayama's lemma says that the lifts generate the maximal ideal. Their number is the dimension of the cotangent space, which equals the Krull dimension by regularity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_quotient_map_etaleCha:
All selected coordinates lie in q, so their ideal J lies in q. The image of q in S/J is a prime. Taking the quotient after localizing at q is the same as localizing S/J at that image prime. Indeed, the images of elements outside q are exactly the elements outside the image prime, by the quotient membership criterion and surjectivity.

The quotient S/J is étale over the polynomial ring in the complementary coordinates by the coordinate quotient construction. Its localization at the image prime is therefore a regular local ring by the regularity result for étale algebras over polynomial rings.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_mvPolynomialCoordIdeal_eq_etaleChart: Extension of an ideal generated by a set takes it to the ideal generated by the images of the set. The polynomial variables indexed by J map to the chart coordinates indexed by J, giving the stated ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_quotient_map_etaleChartCoor:
Induct on the finite set of selected coordinates. The empty set gives the zero ideal, so the quotient has the original dimension. For the induction step, first take the quotient by the ideal generated by the old set. This quotient is regular local. The added coordinate lies in its maximal ideal. Its class is outside the square of that ideal, since membership there would put the original coordinate in the sum of the square of the old maximal ideal and the old coordinate ideal, which the partial derivation argument excludes.

Quotienting a regular local ring by such a parameter lowers the dimension by one. The iterated quotient identifies with the quotient by the ideal generated by the enlarged set. Combining this dimension drop with the induction hypothesis proves the claimed dimension formula.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.coord_restrict: The restricted chart map is the old chart map preceded by the inclusion of V in U. Pulling back a coordinate along this composite is therefore pulling it back along the chart and then restricting its section to V. The global-section identifications with sections on the opens respect these restrictions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.etale_homOfVector_restrictToS: The inverse image of U in the closed subscheme is affine. The ring map for the morphism defined by the surviving coordinates is the quotient chart map, followed by the canonical section-ring isomorphisms. The section ideal of Z is the extension of the selected-variable ideal, so the quotient chart map is étale by the polynomial quotient result. The isomorphisms preserve étaleness. Apply the affine ring criterion to conclude that the morphism is étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.map_mvPolynomialCoordIdeal_eq: Extending the polynomial coordinate ideal sends each variable with index in S to the chart coordinate with that index. Thus the extended ideal is generated by the coordinate sections indexed by S. The ideal of Z over U has these generators by the given equality with the chart ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.restrictToSubscheme_coord: The restricted chart was constructed from the pullbacks of the surviving original coordinates. Pullback of the i-th affine coordinate along that chart gives its i-th defining global section. Translating back to a section on the inverse-image open cancels the initial global-section identification, leaving the specified pullback of the corresponding original coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.restrictToSubscheme_coordIdea:
Work on the affine part of the closed subscheme over U. On U the ideal of E is generated by the original coordinate whose complementary index is i. Pulling back to the closed subscheme and then restricting to the open extends this principal ideal, so the new global ideal is generated by the pullback of that original coordinate.

The singleton ideal in the restricted chart is generated by the pullback of its i-th affine coordinate. By construction of the restricted chart this is the same global section. Thus the two global ideals agree, and they determine the ideal sheaves on this affine scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.X_mem_mvPolynomialCoordIdeal: The variable at j is among the generators because j belongs to S. Every generator lies in the ideal they span.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceGlobalSectionsHom_C: On the polynomial spectrum, the section of the constant polynomial a is the pullback of the scalar a from the spectrum of K under the map induced by the constant inclusion. The affine-space identification takes that map to the affine-space projection. The resulting section is thus the scalar pulled back along the projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceGlobalSectionsHom_X_eq_coord: The inverse affine-space isomorphism pulls the i-th coordinate back to the section for the i-th polynomial variable. Applying pullback along the forward isomorphism reverses this identification, giving the coordinate back.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceGlobalSectionsHom_apply: The map on polynomials first identifies a polynomial with its section on the polynomial spectrum and then pulls that section back to affine space along the canonical isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_comp_hom_apply: Pullback on global sections is contravariant. Applying the pullback along the composite to x amounts to pulling x back along g and then along f.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_comp_specIso_eq_affineSpaceGlobal: The identification of a polynomial with its section on affine space uses pullback along the affine-space isomorphism. The pullback along the composite with F factors into that identification followed by pullback along F, by functoriality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_homOfVector_restrictToSubschemeCo:
Compare the two ring maps on constants and variables. On constants, the morphism defined by the vector of sections has the given structure map. In the quotient formula, renaming preserves the constants, the chart pulls them back through the same structure map, and quotienting restricts them to the closed subscheme. Thus the constants have the same images.

On a smaller-ring variable, the map defined by the vector gives the corresponding component of that vector. In the quotient formula, renaming selects the surviving original coordinate, and the chart sends that variable to its coordinate section. Its class in the quotient is exactly the pullback section used to define the vector component. Agreement on the polynomial generators gives equality of the maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.bijective_commRingCatIso_inv: The forward map is inverse to the inverse isomorphism. Applying the forward map to equal images proves injectivity, and the forward image of any element is a preimage for surjectivity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.bijective_quotientMk_comp_renameCompl: If a renamed polynomial is zero in the quotient, it lies in the coordinate ideal and is killed by the substitution. The substitution recovers the original smaller-ring polynomial, proving injectivity. For surjectivity, start with an arbitrary quotient class and choose a polynomial representing it. Substituting into that representative and then renaming gives the same class, so the smaller polynomial provides a preimage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.card_compl_eq_sub: The set S and its complement partition the m indices. Subtracting the size of S gives the size of the complement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.commRingCatIso_hom_inv_apply: Applying the inverse ring isomorphism and then the forward map to x returns x.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.commRingCatIso_inv_hom_apply: Applying the ring isomorphism and then its inverse to x returns x.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.complOrderEmb_notMem: The order embedding lists precisely the indices in the complement of S. Its value at i is therefore outside S.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordRingHom_apply: The coordinate-ring map on a polynomial is obtained by taking the corresponding affine-space section, pulling it back along the chart, and identifying it with a section over U. This is its defining value at x.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_homOfVector_of_appTop_etale: Identify the affine source with the spectrum of its global sections and the target with the spectrum of the polynomial ring. Naturality of the affine identifications expresses the map defined by the vector of sections as the spectrum map of the indicated ring map under these isomorphisms. The spectrum map is étale by the ring hypothesis, and the affine identifications preserve étaleness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_quotientMap:
Write J for the extension of I in A. The quotient A/J is the base change of A along the projection from P to P/I. To see this, send a pure tensor with factors the class of x and an element a of A to the class of f(x)a. This respects the tensor relations, and every class in A/J is obtained by taking the first factor to be 1.

In the other direction, take the class of a to the tensor of 1 with a. This is well defined because the image of every element of I in the right factor can be moved to its zero class in the left factor, so the map kills J. The two compositions are identities on quotient classes and on pure tensors by the balancing relation. The tensor product is étale over P/I by base change. Transporting along the isomorphism proves étaleness of the induced quotient map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_quotientMk_comp_renameCompl: The map first identifies the smaller polynomial ring with the quotient by the selected variables, then applies the induced quotient map to A/J. The first map is an isomorphism by the complement substitution argument. The second is étale by base change of f to the quotient, since J is the extended ideal. Thus their composite is étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_specMap_of_etale: For a map of rings, the induced map of spectra is étale whenever the ring map is étale. Apply the affine ring criterion to the given map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_complOrderEmb_eq: An index outside S belongs to the complement. The increasing enumeration has that complement as its image, so the index occurs in the enumeration.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isAffineOpen_preimage_subschemeι: The inclusion of a closed subscheme is affine. The inverse image of an affine open under an affine morphism is affine.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iso_hom_appTop_inv_appTop_apply: Pullback takes the composite of an isomorphism with its inverse to the composite of their pullbacks in reverse order. The scheme composite is the identity, so this composite of pullbacks fixes x.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialCoordIdeal_eq_span: The polynomial coordinate ideal is defined as the ideal generated by the variables whose indices lie in S.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.opens_ι_appLE_top_eq_topIso_inv: The section map of the open inclusion views a section over V as a global section on the open subscheme V. This is the inverse of the canonical identification in the other direction. The restriction maps used in the description agree by functoriality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.presheaf_map_comp_eq: Functoriality writes the composite of the two restriction maps as the restriction along the composite arrow. The direct arrow equals it because arrows between the given opens are unique, so their restriction maps agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quotientMk_renameCompl_setCoordsZero: Check the two homomorphisms on the variables. For a variable indexed by S the substitution gives zero, and the original variable is already zero in the quotient. For a variable outside S the substitution takes it to its complementary index and renaming restores the original variable. Both maps preserve scalars, so they agree on every polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.renameCompl_C: Renaming the variables is a homomorphism of k-algebras, so it sends each scalar to the same constant polynomial in the target.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.renameCompl_X: The renaming map substitutes for a smaller-ring variable the original variable at the corresponding position in the increasing enumeration of the complement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_subschemeι_eq_top: The restriction of the pulled-back ideal to the inverse image of U is obtained by first restricting E to U and then pulling it back along the restricted closed immersion. The restriction to U is the unit ideal by hypothesis, and its pullback is also the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictToSubscheme_map_appTop_coord: The morphism of the restricted chart is built from the vector of surviving coordinate sections. Pullback of the i-th affine coordinate gives the i-th component of this vector, the pullback of the corresponding original coordinate viewed as a global section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.setCoordsZero_X_complOrderEmb: The original variable at the indicated index survives because that index lies outside S. The substitution sends it to the variable at the unique preimage of that index under the increasing enumeration. Injectivity of the enumeration identifies the preimage with i.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.setCoordsZero_X_of_mem: Evaluate the substitution at the variable with index j. The rule sends it to zero because j belongs to S.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.setCoordsZero_eq_zero_of_mem: The substitution kills all variables with indices in S. Their generated ideal lies in its kernel, so the substitution sends q to zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.setCoordsZero_renameCompl: A variable in the smaller ring is renamed to the corresponding surviving original index, then sent back to the starting variable by the substitution. The two maps preserve scalars. Equality on the variables and scalars gives the identity on every polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeι_appLE_apply: For the closed subscheme over the affine open U, its section ring is the quotient of the section ring on U by the ideal defining it there. Pulling a section back along the closed immersion sends it to its class in that quotient, transported to the section ring of the inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeι_appLE_topIso_hom_appTop_apply: The first pullback gives the restriction along q to U. Pulling that section back to the inverse image of U under the closed immersion combines with the first restriction to give the restriction along the composite. Converting the resulting section to a global section on the inverse-image open gives precisely the pullback along its structure map.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algHom_map_derivation_eq_zero: If r maps to zero, it belongs to the kernel, which is the principal ideal of h. The derivation preserves that ideal because it kills h. Thus the derivative of r also belongs to the kernel and maps to zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_flat: Multiplication by r is injective on R because r is a non-zero-divisor. After tensoring with the flat algebra A this remains injective and becomes multiplication by the image of r. Hence that image is a non-zero-divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coord_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isAffineOpe: A polynomial variable is a nonzero element of the polynomial domain over k, hence a non-zero-divisor. The chart ring map is étale and therefore flat. Its image of the variable is the chart coordinate and remains a non-zero-divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivation_mapsTo_span_self: An element of the principal ideal is a multiple of h. In the product rule for its derivative, the term involving the derivative of h vanishes. The remaining term is again divisible by h, so the derivative stays in the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.det_eq_det_submatrix_of_col_eq_single: Transpose the matrix so the specified column becomes a row. The row result applies, and the resulting submatrix is the transpose of the desired minor. The determinant is invariant under transpose both for the original matrix and for the minor, giving the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.det_eq_det_submatrix_of_row_eq_single: Reindex the rows and columns by the same bijection so that the specified row becomes the first row. Simultaneous reindexing preserves the determinant. The first row now has a 1 in the first column and zeros elsewhere. Expanding there gives the determinant after deleting that row and column, which is the stated submatrix in the original indices.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.det_eq_det_submatrix_succ: Expand the determinant along its first row. The off-diagonal entries of this row are zero. Its diagonal entry is 1 and its cofactor sign is positive. The remaining determinant is the minor obtained by deleting the first row and first column.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_unit_mul_coord_of_span_eq: The chart coordinate is a non-zero-divisor on the affine open. The equality of principal ideals therefore satisfies the unit-multiple criterion with the chart coordinate as b. It expresses g as a unit times that coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_unit_mul_of_span_eq: Equality of the principal ideals gives elements c and d with a equal to cb and b equal to da. Substituting the first equality into the second gives that dc times b equals b. Since b is a non-zero-divisor, cancellation gives dc equal to 1. In a commutative ring this makes c a unit with inverse d, so a is the asserted unit multiple of b.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.liftDerivationOfKerEqSpan_apply: The previous kernel calculation makes the derivative of a representative well defined under the quotient map. Specifically, two preimages of the same element differ by an element of the kernel, whose derivative still lies in the kernel. The descended derivation therefore takes the class of r to the class of its derivative, as stated.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.ofCoords_map: The chart built from the vector of sections uses the affine-space morphism associated to that vector as its underlying map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.restrict_map: Restriction of a chart is defined by precomposing its map with the inclusion of the smaller open. This yields the stated map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_homOfLE_comp_topIso_hom: Identify the global sections of the open subschemes with the sections over the corresponding opens of X. Under these identifications, pullback along the inclusion is restriction from V to W. The two composites of restriction maps agree by functoriality, since they come from the same inclusion of opens.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_homOfLE_comp_map: The inclusion of V into U is an open immersion and is therefore étale. Its composite with the étale chart map is étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart:
Choose an affine open V containing x. The structure map on its section ring is smooth over k. Standard smoothness holds after localizing at a family of elements that generates the unit ideal. The basic opens of this family cover V, so one of them, U, contains x. Its section ring is the indicated localization, and the scalar map there is the restriction of the scalar map on V. Hence U has a standard smooth presentation over k.

Use the presentation result to choose polynomial coordinates whose evaluation in the global section ring of U is étale. Taking spectra gives an étale map from U to affine space under the canonical affine identifications. The evaluation sends constants to the structure map on U. On spectra this says that the affine-space projection composed with the chart is the restriction of p, completing the chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart_le: Take an affine chart neighbourhood of x. Inside its intersection with W, choose a basic open containing x using the basic-open basis of the affine chart domain. This smaller open is affine and contained in W. Restrict the chart along its inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etale_eval₂Hom_of_submersivePrese:
The presentation chooses a distinct generator for each relation, and the Jacobian in those generators is invertible after evaluation in S. Use the complementary generators as variables of a polynomial base ring over k. The original polynomial ring can now be written in two blocks, with the chosen generators as variables and the complementary variables in the coefficient ring.

Rewrite the relations in this two-block presentation. The map from the original polynomial ring to the new presentation ring is surjective because every scalar and every variable in either block has a preimage. Evaluation of the rewritten polynomials in S agrees with the original evaluation on all generators. Hence the rewritten relations still generate the kernel: the new evaluation pulls back to the old evaluation, and extending the old kernel along the surjection gives the new one.

Differentiation in a chosen generator commutes with the change of presentation. On variables this holds because complementary generators are now coefficients and have derivative zero in the chosen directions, and it extends by linearity and the product rule. Thus the new Jacobian matrix comes from the old one by applying the rewrite entrywise. Its determinant evaluates to the old unit in S. The new presentation has equally many variables and equations over the polynomial base and has invertible Jacobian, so it is standard smooth of relative dimension zero and hence étale. Its base map sends the complementary variables to their given values in S, as required.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_basicOpen_of_span_eq_top: Suppose x belongs to none of the basic opens defined by the sections in s. Then the germ of every such section is a nonunit and lies in the maximal ideal of the local ring at x. The contraction of that ideal to the section ring would contain s and hence the ideal it generates. Since s generates the unit ideal, the contraction would contain 1, which is impossible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.homOfLE_comp_map_comp_affineSpaceFinToSp: The original chart composed with the projection to the spectrum of k is the restriction of p to U. Precompose with the inclusion from V to U. The two successive open inclusions give the inclusion of V in X, so the resulting structure map is the restriction of p to V.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.homOfVector_comp_affineSpaceFinToSpec: The morphism associated to the vector of sections is constructed over the given structure map of U. Composing with the affine-space projection therefore recovers that structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.opens_op_hom_ext: An arrow between two opens just expresses an inclusion, so there is at most one arrow with the given endpoints. The same holds after reversing the arrows.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.presheaf_map_eq: The two arrows agree because they have the same endpoints in the category of opens. Applying the presheaf sends them to equal ring maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_ΓSpecIso_inv_comp_appTop: The inclusion of V is an open immersion, so its composite with p is smooth. Because V is affine, identify it with the spectrum of its global section ring. Under this identification the structure map is induced by the map from k to those sections. Smoothness of a map between affine schemes is equivalent to smoothness of the corresponding ring map, giving the claim.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceFin_hom_ext: A map to affine space over the spectrum of K is determined by its composite to that base and the pullbacks of the coordinate functions. The two hypotheses identify these data for f and g, so the affine-space universal property gives equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_comp_apply: Global sections are contravariant in the scheme. Pulling a section back along the composite first pulls it back along g and then along f, giving the stated equality on the section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartPullbackFstStalkMap_eq: The first projection sends the chosen fibre-product point to p. The first map on local rings is defined by this identification of the source stalk followed by the map induced by the first projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartPullbackFst_base_chartPullbackPoint: The fibre-product point is the image of the unique point of the residue-field spectrum. By the first projection identity it maps to the point of V lying over p, and the inclusion of V takes that point to p.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartPullbackFst_comp_eq_chartPullbackSn: The two maps from the fibre product to affine space agree. Compose them with its structure map to the spectrum of k. For each chart the resulting composite also factors through the open inclusion of V in P followed by q, giving the claimed equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartPullbackLift_fst: Agreement of the charts on the residue field permits the two copies of the residue-field point to define a map into the fibre product. By its defining property, the first projection of this map is the first of those copies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartPullbackLift_fst_assoc: Compose the first projection identity for the residue-field lift with g. Associativity identifies this with the stated composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartPullbackLift_snd: The lift is formed from two copies of the canonical map from the residue field to V. Composing the lift with the second projection recovers the second copy.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartPullbackLift_snd_assoc: Compose the second projection identity for the residue-field lift with g and reassociate the maps.
