Thus the neighbourhood lies in T. Every point has such an open neighbourhood inside T, proving that T is also open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isDomain_localization_of_iso_spec: The point y corresponds under the affine identification to a prime of R. The localization of R at this prime identifies with the stalk on its spectrum and hence with the local ring at y. The latter is a domain by hypothesis, so the localization is also a domain.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isDomain_stalk_of_smooth: The local ring at x is regular by the preceding theorem. Every regular local ring is an integral domain.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherianRing_sections_of_isAffineOpe: The global section ring of V is a finite type algebra over k by the preceding result. A field is Noetherian, and a finite type algebra over a Noetherian ring is Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isReduced_of_smooth: Every stalk is a domain by smoothness and therefore has no nonzero nilpotent elements. Reducedness can be checked on stalks, proving that X is reduced.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_of_flat_formallyUnram: The dimensions of the two local rings agree by the preceding argument. The maximal ideal of S is the extension of the maximal ideal of R by formal unramifiedness and essential finite type. It needs at most as many generators, which by regularity of R is the common dimension. The height bound in the Noetherian local ring S gives the reverse inequality on the generator count. Equality is the criterion for regularity of S.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_stalk_affineSpace: Affine space is the spectrum of the coordinate polynomial ring over k. A polynomial ring in finitely many variables over a field is regular at each prime. Applying the comparison with the localizations at these primes gives the result for the stalk.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_iso_spec: The isomorphism sends x to a prime of R. The stalk at that point on the spectrum is the localization at that prime. It is regular by hypothesis. The isomorphism identifies it with the stalk at x, which is therefore regular.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_opens: An open inclusion induces an isomorphism on the corresponding local rings. Transport regularity of the local ring of the open subscheme across this isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth: Choose an étale chart around x. The local ring of the affine-space target at the image point is regular. The map on stalks induced by the chart is local, flat, essentially of finite type, and formally unramified, so the local algebra criterion makes the source stalk regular. The chart domain is an open neighbourhood of x, and its local ring at x agrees with the ambient one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_stalkMap_fla: The map on the two stalks is local. The source stalk is Noetherian by its regularity, and the target stalk is Noetherian because the map is essentially of finite type. The local algebra regularity theorem applies using flatness, formal unramifiedness, and essential finite type.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_eq_of_flat_formallyUnramifi: Flatness gives going-down, so the dimension of S is at least that of R. For a formally unramified local map essentially of finite type, the maximal ideal of the target is the extension of the maximal ideal of the source. The preceding generator bound then gives the opposite dimension inequality because R is regular.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_le_of_hasGoingDown: In the base local ring, the last prime of any finite prime chain lies inside the maximal ideal. Under a local ring map this maximal ideal is the contraction of the maximal ideal of S. Going-down lifts the chain to S with the same length, using that maximal ideal as the bound. Every prime chain length in R is therefore bounded by the dimension of S. Taking the supremum gives the inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_le_of_map_maximalIdeal: In the Noetherian local ring S, the height of its maximal ideal is its Krull dimension and is bounded by the minimal number of generators of that ideal. The displayed extension formula bounds this generator count by that of the maximal ideal of R. Regularity of R identifies that count with its dimension, giving the claimed inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_isDomain_stalk: The supplied smoothness gives regularity of the local ring at x, hence that ring is a domain.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_isReduced: Apply the reducedness result for schemes smooth over a field using the given smoothness proof for p.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_isRegularLocalRing_stalk: Apply the regularity result on stalks of a smooth scheme to the supplied smoothness of p and the point x.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.spanFinrank_map_le: Choose a generating set of least size for I. It is finite because R is Noetherian. Its image generates the extended ideal in S and has at most as many elements as the original set. The minimal number of generators of the extension is bounded by this size.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_C_map_C: A constant polynomial belongs to the extended ideal exactly when all its coefficients belong to I. Its only possibly nonzero coefficient is the original scalar, so membership is equivalent to that scalar belonging to I. This identifies the contraction with I.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_comap_symm: Contraction of an ideal twice is contraction along the composite of the two ring maps in the appropriate order. Here the composite applies the isomorphism and then its inverse, so it is the identity on A. The contracted ideal is I.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_symm_comap: The double contraction is along the composite that applies the inverse isomorphism and then the isomorphism. This is the identity on B and returns J.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_fromSpecStalkPoint_eq_of_speciali: The image of the spectrum of the local ring at x consists exactly of the generizations of x. Since y specializes to x, it has a preimage in that spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isClosed_singleton_of_isAffine: Identify the affine scheme with the spectrum of its global section ring. Extend the prime corresponding to a to a maximal ideal. Its point is closed in the spectrum and remains closed under the affine homeomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isClosed_singleton_of_isAffineOpe: A point of U exists by nonemptiness. The open subscheme U is affine, so the result for a nonempty affine scheme gives a closed point of U.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_ltSeries_comap: Contract every prime in the given chain along the ring isomorphism. Contraction preserves inclusion, and it reflects equality because contraction along the inverse isomorphism recovers the original prime. Thus strict inclusions remain strict. The new chain has the same length and its last prime is the contraction of the given last prime.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_ltSeries_of_isMaximal_mvPolynomia:
Induct on the number of variables. For zero variables the maximal ideal itself is a chain of length zero. For the successor step, view the ring as a polynomial ring in one variable over the ring with n variables. The smaller ring is Jacobson because it is of finite type over a field, so the contraction N of the given maximal ideal is maximal. By induction there is a chain of length n ending at N.

Extend the primes in that chain to the one-variable polynomial ring. Extension preserves primality because the quotient by an extended prime is a polynomial ring over a domain. It preserves strict inclusion because contracting along constants recovers the original ideals. The last extended prime is contained in the given maximal ideal and is strictly smaller by the preceding result. Append the maximal ideal and transport the chain back along the polynomial-ring isomorphism.

Reindex the variables by the bijection with the ordinary finite index set. The maximal ideal corresponds to a maximal ideal in the ordinary polynomial ring, where the preceding result gives the chain. Contraction along the isomorphism transports the chain back, preserving its length and recovering the original maximal ideal at its end.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_isClosed_singleton_of_isAffin: Choose a closed point of the affine open subscheme U by the preceding result. It consists of a point of X together with its membership in U. Take those data and the closedness proof in U.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.fromSpecStalkPoint_specializes_iff: The canonical map from the spectrum of the local ring at x into X is a topological embedding. An embedding preserves and reflects specialization, giving the equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaximal_comap_C: Over a Jacobson base the map from S to the quotient by the maximal polynomial ideal is integral. The quotient is a field, so contraction of its zero maximal ideal is maximal in S. That contraction is exactly the contraction of the given polynomial ideal along the constants.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_ringKrullDim_stalk_affineSpace: Under the identification with the polynomial spectrum, the closed point corresponds to a maximal ideal. The polynomial prime-chain result gives a chain of length m ending at that ideal. Transporting this chain to affine space gives distinct points ordered by specialization, all specializing to x. The stalk chain criterion therefore gives dimension at least m.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_ringKrullDim_stalk_of_chain: Each point in the specialization chain is a generization of x, so lift it to the spectrum of the stalk at x. The embedding reflects each specialization as inclusion of the lifted primes. The given points are distinct, so adjacent inclusions of primes are strict. This gives a prime chain of length n in the stalk and hence the lower bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_C_ne_of_isMaximal: If the extension of N were the maximal ideal M′, the polynomial variable would be outside M′, since its coefficient of degree one is 1 outside N. In the field quotient by M′ its class would have an inverse. Thus some polynomial times the variable would agree with 1 modulo the ideal extended from N. Taking constant coefficients forces 1 to lie in N, since the polynomial times the variable has zero constant coefficient. This contradicts that N is proper.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_mvPolynomial_uLift_le: The two index sets are bijective, so renaming the variables gives an isomorphism to the polynomial ring in m variables. Ring isomorphisms preserve Krull dimension, and that polynomial ring over the field has dimension m.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_of_etale: The étale morphism induces a local map from the stalk on W to the stalk on Y which is flat, formally unramified, and essentially of finite type. Apply the local dimension equality theorem, using regularity of the stalk on W and Noetherianity of the stalk on Y.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_of_etale_affineSpa: The dimension of the stalk at y is at most m by the affine-space bound. An étale map to affine space over a field takes a closed point to a closed point by the closed-point result. Thus the target stalk at the image of y has dimension at least m by the prime-chain construction. Its dimension equals the source stalk dimension by the étale comparison, giving equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_le_of_etale: The map on stalks of the étale morphism is local, flat, essentially of finite type, and formally unramified. The source and target rings of this local map satisfy the regularity and Noetherian hypotheses of the dimension equality theorem. Their dimensions are therefore equal, giving the asserted inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_le_of_etale_affineSpa: The affine-space stalk at the image is regular. The étale stalk dimension comparison bounds the dimension at y by the dimension of that target stalk. The target stalk dimension is bounded by the dimension of the whole affine space via the embedding of its spectrum, and the affine space has dimension m by its polynomial description.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_le_topologicalKrullDi: The ring dimension of the local ring equals the topological dimension of its spectrum. The canonical map embeds this spectrum into X, and the topological dimension of the embedded subspace is bounded by that of X.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specializes_of_fromSpecStalk_base_specia: The canonical map from the stalk spectrum is a topological embedding. Apply reflection of specialization to the two image points.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_affineSpace_le_ringK: The affine-space isomorphism identifies it with the spectrum of the coordinate polynomial ring. The topological dimension equals that of this spectrum, which is the ring dimension of the polynomial ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_forall_ringKru:
Take any strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of X. Choose the generic point of each subset. Inclusions in the chain give specializations from the larger subsets' generic points to the smaller ones. Distinct closed subsets have distinct generic points.

All these generic points are generizations of the generic point of the smallest subset, so they lift to the spectrum of the local ring there. The embedding reflects specialization, and the distinctness of the image points gives strictness. In reverse order the lifted points form a prime chain of the same length. The local dimension bound therefore bounds the length of the original chain. Taking the supremum over the chains gives the topological bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_spec_le_ringKrullDim: The topological Krull dimension of the prime spectrum of a ring equals the ring's Krull dimension. The displayed inequality follows.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.coordIdeal_eq_comap_coordSubs: The chart ideal for S is defined by pulling back the coordinate subspace ideal for S along the chart's étale map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.HasStrictNormalCrossingsWith.exists_etal: Apply the defining local condition of h at the given point x of the support of Z. This supplies the chart, the assignment for E, and the coordinate set for Z with all the required properties.

At x, choose the local chart, the coordinate set S for Z, and the assignment b for the full list H :: E. Keep the chart and S. Assign b(0) to H and b(i+1) to the i-th entry of E. The old ideal conditions at index 0 give the two possibilities for H. At index i+1 they give the two possibilities for the corresponding tail entry.

If a tail entry uses the coordinate assigned to H, injectivity on the assigned coordinates gives i+1 = 0, which is impossible. If two tail entries use the same coordinate, injectivity gives i+1 = j+1 and hence i = j. The original ideal condition for Z applies to the retained chart and S.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.InStrictNormalCrossingPositionAt.exists_: Unfold the local condition at x. Its witnesses are the neighbourhood, chart, and coordinate assignment, and its three requirements give exactly the desired properties.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coordSubspaceIdeal_eq_ofIdealTop_span_co: Take the coordinate functions indexed by S in the coordinate ring of the affine space. The coordinate subspace ideal sheaf is defined by taking the sheaf associated to the ring ideal they generate, giving the displayed formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_iff: Unfold the condition at a point x of the support of Z. It asks for an étale coordinate chart around x and an assignment of optional coordinate indices to the entries of E. An unassigned entry restricts to the unit ideal, and an assigned entry restricts to the corresponding coordinate hyperplane ideal. Distinct assigned entries use distinct coordinates. In the same chart, Z restricts to the ideal of the coordinates indexed by S. These are exactly the witnesses and conditions on the right.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_of_forall_e: For each x in the support of Z, the hypothesis supplies a chart with distinct coordinate indices for the assigned entries of E and the required coordinate ideal for Z. These pointwise data give the defining condition for strict normal crossings along Z.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPositionAt_of_exis: Use the given neighbourhood, chart, and assignment in the definition at x. The three conditions in the hypothesis say that assigned indices are distinct and determine the restrictions of every assigned or unassigned entry of E.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_iff: By definition, the global condition consists of smoothness of each divisor in E and the local chart condition at every point of X. Unfolding it gives exactly the stated conjunction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_iff: The definition imposes two conditions. The ideal D is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor, and the subscheme cut out by D is smooth over the base via its inclusion followed by p. These are the two conditions on the right.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_iff: The definition requires each irreducible component to have a point outside the support of I. This is precisely the stated condition that no component is contained in that support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_eq_comap_resLE_restr: Since f sends V into U, the two composites V → X → Y and V → U → Y agree, with V → U the restriction of f. Pullback of I along the first composite restricts the pullback along f. Pullback along the second composite pulls back the restriction of I to U. Functoriality identifies the two ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_eq_comap_homOfLE_restrictI: The inclusion V → X is the composite V → U → X. Pullback along this composite first restricts I to U and then pulls that restricted ideal back to V. This is also the direct restriction of I to V.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_eq_comap_ι: The restriction of I to U is defined by pulling back I along the open immersion U → X. This is exactly the ideal on the right.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_eq_of_le_of_eq: Express the two restrictions to V as pullbacks along V → U. Their inputs are the equal restrictions of I and J to U, so the pullbacks agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_eq_top_iff_forall_notMem_s: An ideal sheaf is the unit ideal exactly when its support is empty. The support of the pullback to U is the inverse image of the support of I under U → X. A point of U is a point x of X with x ∈ U, and it belongs to that inverse image exactly when x belongs to the support of I. Thus the restricted ideal is the unit ideal exactly when every point of U avoids the support of I.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.vanishesAlong_iff_le: Vanishing of I along J is defined to mean that I is contained in J. Both directions are the identity on this condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.zeroLocus_eq_support: The zero locus of an ideal sheaf is defined to be its support as a closed subset of X.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.pullbackOpenImmersion_map: The pulled-back chart uses the map from the inverse-image open to V followed by the original chart map. This is its defining underlying map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.complInv_def: The partial inverse is undefined on indices in S. For any other index it returns that index's chosen position in the increasing enumeration of the complement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.complInv_eq_some_iff: If the partial inverse returns j, the original index is outside S and j is by construction a preimage under the complement enumeration. Conversely, if the enumeration sends j to t, then t is outside S. Its chosen preimage must be j by injectivity of the enumeration, so the partial inverse returns j.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_none_of_bind_complInv_eq_none: If the original assignment contained an index, the hypothesis would put that index in the complement. The partial inverse is defined at every complementary index, so the result would contain an entry. Thus the original assignment was empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_some_and_not_of_bind_ite_eq_some: The filter can return j only from an original entry. It retains that entry exactly when its predicate is false. Thus the original entry is j and it fails the predicate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_some_complOrderEmb_of_bind_complInv_e: An empty original entry could not produce j. For an original entry t, the partial inverse returns j exactly when the complement enumeration sends j to t. Hence the original entry is the index at position j in that enumeration.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_top_of_forall_ideal_eq_top: An ideal sheaf is determined by its ideals on affine opens. The unit ideal sheaf assigns the whole section ring on each affine open, which agrees everywhere with the given sheaf.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_morphismRestrict_comp_map: Restricting the open immersion f to the inverse image of V gives an open immersion into V. It is étale, and the original chart is étale. Their composite is therefore étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart_coord_mem_primeIdealOf:
Let t be the product of the chart coordinates outside the prime at y. Since the complement of the prime is multiplicatively closed, t stays outside it, and its affine basic open still contains y. Restrict the chart to this open. Every coordinate appearing in t is invertible there because each is a factor of the product being inverted.

Delete from the assignment every coordinate outside the prime. An originally unassigned ideal is still the unit ideal after restriction. An ideal whose coordinate was deleted is now the unit ideal because that generator became invertible. For retained coordinates the coordinate-ideal description persists under restriction. The assignment remains injective because the retained values are a subset of the old ones.

Finally, any retained coordinate belongs to the original prime and hence vanishes at y. The corresponding ideal has y in its support. On the smaller affine open it is again generated by the restricted coordinate, so the support criterion puts this generator in the prime at y there.

First construct the chart on T using the component condition. Regard the divisors as the list of ideals pulled back to T, preserving their positions. Apply the chart normalization at y to this list. It supplies an affine chart with the same two alternatives for each ideal and with every assigned coordinate in the prime at y. Expressing each entry again as the pullback of the corresponding original divisor gives the stated witnesses.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart_on_open_of_hasStrictNo:
Take a common strict normal crossing chart for the centre Z and the divisors at the image of y, and shrink to an affine neighbourhood. Let S be the coordinates cutting out the centre. Suppose a divisor is assigned a coordinate in S. Its ideal is then contained in the ideal of Z on this neighbourhood, so every point of Z there lies in the divisor support. In particular this holds for the image of the part of the irreducible component of T through y lying over the neighbourhood. That part is nonempty and open in the component. Its image lying in the closed support forces the whole component's image into that support by irreducibility and continuity. This contradicts the component hypothesis. Every assigned divisor coordinate is therefore outside S.

Restrict the chart to the closed subscheme by keeping the complementary coordinates. Pull this chart back along the open inclusion of T, then shrink to an affine neighbourhood of y. For the divisor list, translate each assigned complementary coordinate to its position in the new chart and leave each unassigned entry empty. The singleton ideal formula identifies assigned divisors with the new coordinate ideals, and the unit ideal remains the unit ideal under pullback and restriction. Distinctness of assigned coordinates follows from distinctness in the original chart and the bijection with the complement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_subset_of_image_inter_subset: Every open neighbourhood of a point of A meets A. Irreducibility says that such a neighbourhood and O have a common point in A, since O also meets A. Hence A lies in the closure of its intersection with O. The inverse image of the closed set C under the continuous map g is closed and contains that intersection, so it contains A. This gives the claimed inclusion of images.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_basicOpen_iff_notMem_primeIdealOf: The affine identification takes x to its corresponding prime and takes the basic open of f to the basic open of the same ring element on the spectrum. A prime lies in this basic open precisely when it does not contain f.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_primeIdealOf_of_mem_support_of_ideal: The generator g is a section in the ideal. Since x is in the support, this section vanishes there, so x lies outside its basic open. Under the affine identification that means the prime at x contains g.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_iff_forall_notMem_basicOpen: On the affine open U, the support of the ideal sheaf is the common zero locus of its section ideal. A section vanishes at x precisely when the basic open it defines misses x. Applying this to every section in the ideal gives the equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_of_ideal_eq_span_singleton: Every section in the ideal on U is a multiple of g. The basic open of a multiple is contained in the basic open of g. Since x lies in none of these opens, it belongs to the common zero locus of the ideal, hence to its support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.morphismRestrict_comp_map_comp_affineSpa: After the original chart and its affine-space projection, the map from V to the spectrum of k is its inclusion followed by p. Precompose this identity with the restriction of f. The square of open restrictions identifies its composite with the inclusion of the inverse-image open followed by f and p.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.of_bind_ite_eq_none: The original entry is j. If the predicate were false at j, the filter would retain it. Since the result is empty, the predicate holds.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_eq_coordIdeal_pullba: The coordinate ideal of the pulled-back chart is the pullback of the original chart ideal along the restricted map to V, because both are defined from the same coordinate subspace ideal. By hypothesis the original chart ideal equals the restriction of D. Pullback of that restriction agrees with restriction of the pulled-back ideal because the square of open restrictions commutes.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_preimage_eq_top: Restricting the pullback to the inverse-image open is the same as pulling back the restriction to V. That restriction is the unit ideal by hypothesis, and its pullback is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_eq_top_of_le_basicOpen: On any affine open of the open subscheme V, the restricted ideal is generated by the image of f. The section f is invertible on its basic open, and its restriction to V and then to the chosen affine open remains invertible. The extended principal ideal is therefore the whole section ring. These affine ideals determine the unit ideal sheaf.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeι_base_mem_support_of_subscheme: The image of the closed immersion defined by Z is the support of Z. In particular the image of z lies in that support.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etaleChartCoord_eq_coord: In the algebra associated to the chart, its j-th coordinate is the image of the j-th polynomial variable. The chart's coordinate-ring map sends that variable to the pullback of the j-th affine-space coordinate, which is the coordinate section of the chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_finset_comap_prod_ideal_eq_span_p:
Induct on the list of ideals. The empty list gives the unit ideal, generated by the empty product. For a nonempty list, shift the coordinate assignment by one position to apply induction to the tail. This gives a finite set of tail coordinates and a principal generator equal to their product.

The ideal of the pulled-back full product on V is the product of the pulled-back head ideal and tail ideal. An unassigned head gives the unit ideal and leaves the tail product as the generator. If the head is assigned a coordinate, its ideal on V is generated by that coordinate. Injectivity of the assignment prevents this coordinate from occurring in the tail set. Adjoin it, and multiply the two principal generators. Every index in the resulting set comes from an assigned list entry.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_comap_mul: On V, the pulled-back ideal from U is obtained by ideal extension along the map of section rings. The product sheaf on U gives the product of the two section ideals, and ideal extension preserves products. This gives the product of the two extensions on V.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_top_of_isAffineOpen_of_restrict: Under the isomorphism between sections over V in Y and global sections of the open subscheme V, the ideal on V extends to the ideal of the restricted sheaf. By hypothesis that extension is the whole ring. Pulling the whole ring back along the isomorphism gives the whole section ring of V, so the ideal on V is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_top: The unit ideal sheaf assigns the whole section ring as its ideal on each affine open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.presheaf_map_mem_primeIdealOf: On an affine neighbourhood of x, a section belongs to the prime corresponding to x exactly when its germ belongs to the maximal ideal of the local ring. The germ of the restricted section on V′ agrees with the original germ on V. Apply this criterion in both affine neighbourhoods to transfer membership.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictNormalCrossingsRestrictToClopen:
Smoothness of the centre follows from its strict normal crossing charts. Its open subscheme T is therefore smooth over the field, so the local ring at y is regular. Choose the chart on T where each restricted divisor is either the unit ideal or generated by a distinct coordinate that vanishes at y. Choose an affine neighbourhood of the image of y in W and shrink the chart to a basic affine open V inside its inverse image. Restricting to V preserves the ideal descriptions, and the coordinate germs at y are the same as before.

The product of the pulled-back divisor ideals on V is generated by the product of the selected coordinates. Each selected coordinate lies in the prime of y. The ideal of their product is radical by the reducedness result for a product of distinct étale chart coordinates. The coordinate ring of V is nonzero because the point y gives a proper prime. In that ring distinct chart coordinates are different sections.

Extend the selected coordinate sections to sections whose germs form a regular system of parameters at y. Choose a parameter index representing each selected coordinate. Two selected coordinates with the same parameter index would be equal as sections, so the index choice is injective. The product of the selected coordinates is therefore the product of the corresponding subset of parameter sections. Taking the radical has no effect on this ideal. These sections and their selected indices give the required strict normal crossing witnesses.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.top_le_ι_preimage_self: Every point of the open subscheme V has image in V by definition of the inclusion. The preimage of V is therefore the whole open subscheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ι_appLE_top_bijective: The section map is the inverse of the canonical section-ring isomorphism. In particular it is injective and surjective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ι_appLE_top_eq_topIso_inv: A section on V viewed as an open of Y becomes a global section of the open subscheme V by the restriction identification. This direction is the inverse of the canonical isomorphism from global sections of the open subscheme to sections on V.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPositionAt_nil: Smoothness supplies an étale chart on an open neighbourhood of x. Use the assignment that selects no coordinate at any index. The empty list has no valid indices, so the distinctness and both ideal conditions hold vacuously.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_nil: There are no divisors in the list to check for smoothness. At each point the preceding local result supplies the required étale chart for the empty list.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor.of_isOpen: Given a point of X, choose a preimage in one of the open immersions. The strict normal crossing witnesses for the pulled-back divisor at that point transport to X by the local open-immersion lemma. This supplies the required witnesses at every point of X.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor.reducedIn: The two open summands cover the coproduct. On either summand, the pullback of the reduced inverse image is the reduced inverse image under the restricted map, by the open-immersion formula. The two hypotheses give strict normal crossings on these summands, so the result follows by the open-cover criterion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.closedPreimage_coe: The inverse image of the closed set S is closed by continuity. The definition uses that inverse image as the underlying set of the resulting closed subset of X′.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_ideal_radical_eq_of_isOpenImmersio: The image of the affine open V under the open immersion is affine and isomorphic to V. On V the pulled-back ideal is the extension of the ideal on the image along the corresponding isomorphism of section rings. The ideal on the image is radical because the original sheaf is radical. Its extension along the ring isomorphism is radical by the ring-level result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_reducedInverseImage_of_isOpenImmer: Write the reduced inverse image under f as the vanishing ideal sheaf of the inverse image of W. Pullback along the open immersion gives the vanishing ideal sheaf of the further inverse image. The two successive inverse images are the inverse image under the composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_vanishingIdeal_of_isOpenImmersion: The vanishing ideal sheaf of Z is radical. Its pullback under the open immersion is radical on each affine open and hence radical as an ideal sheaf. The support of the pullback is the inverse image of Z by the support formula. A radical ideal sheaf is the vanishing ideal sheaf of its support, giving the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_vanishingIdeal_of_isOpenImmersion_: The assumed equality of underlying sets identifies Z′ with the closed inverse image of Z. Substitute this identification in the pullback formula for vanishing ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_span_of_map_eq_span: Extend the equality of ideals along ψ. The composite ψ after φ is the identity, so the extended image of I returns to I. The image of the principal ideal generated by b is the principal ideal generated by ψ(b).
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_appLE_image: The open immersion identifies U with its open image. The map on sections from that image to U is the map induced by this identification and is therefore an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRadical_map_of_bijective: If a power of y belongs to the extended ideal, write y as the image of z under the bijection. Then the image of the same power of z is the image of an element of I. Injectivity shows that this power of z lies in I. Since I is radical, z belongs to I, so y lies in its image ideal. The reverse inclusion is the usual inclusion of an ideal in its radical.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularParameterSystem_of_ringEquiv: The range of the new parameters is the image under e of the old range. Thus the generated ideal is the image of the old maximal ideal, which is the new maximal ideal under the local ring isomorphism. Krull dimension is preserved by a ring isomorphism, so the length of the parameter system is still the dimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictNormalCrossingsAt_base_of_comap:
Take an affine neighbourhood V of x and sections on it that witness strict normal crossings for the pullback ideal. The open immersion identifies V with an affine neighbourhood of the image point and identifies the two local rings. Transport the sections to the image by the inverse of the isomorphism on sections. Compatibility of germs with pullback identifies their germs with the original regular parameters. Regularity of the local ring and the parameter-system conditions are preserved by the stalk isomorphism.

On the affine neighbourhood V, the pulled-back ideal is the extension of the ideal on the image. It is generated by the product of the chosen sections. Transport that generator back along the inverse isomorphism on section rings. The inverse preserves products, so the ideal on the image is generated by the product of the transported sections at the same indices.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reducedInverseImage_comp: A point of A maps into W under the composite exactly when its image in B belongs to the inverse image of W. The two closed sets therefore agree. Take their vanishing ideal sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reducedInverseImage_eq_radical: The support hypothesis identifies the support of J with the closed inverse image. Its vanishing ideal sheaf is the radical of J, which gives the asserted reduced inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.reducedInverseImage_eq_vanishingIdeal_cl: By definition the reduced inverse image is cut out by the vanishing ideal sheaf of the topological inverse image. The closed set in the formula is this inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkMap_germ_eq_germ_appLE: Naturality of the map on local rings sends the germ of s to the germ of its pullback on the full inverse image of U. Taking that germ after restricting the pullback section to V gives the same element, since restriction to a smaller neighbourhood of x preserves the germ.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_vanishingIdeal: The vanishing ideal sheaf of Z defines the reduced closed subscheme supported on Z. Its support as a closed set is therefore Z.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appLE_eq_map_comp_appLE: Pulling back a section from U to V only uses its values over W, since the image of V is contained in W. Compatibility of pullback with restriction identifies the direct map with restriction from U to W followed by pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.base_mem_support_of_mem_support_comap: The support of the pulled-back ideal is the inverse image of the support of I. Thus a point in that support maps into the support of I.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_comp_ringEquiv: Changing the source ring by an isomorphism preserves étaleness. The composite with e is that change of source applied to f.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_of_formallyEtale_of_finitePresenta: A formally étale algebra of finite presentation is étale. The hypotheses give the two conditions for the algebra induced by f.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart_comap_coord_eq: Apply the preceding chart construction at y above U. It gives an affine neighbourhood inside the inverse image of U and an étale chart there with the original coordinates pulled back into the first block. These are the asserted witnesses.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etaleChart_comap_restrictIdeal_eq:
Near y, use smoothness to choose affine opens W contained in U and V above W, with V étale over a relative affine space of dimension d over W. Restrict the original chart to W. The polynomial-ring construction combines its m coordinates with the d relative coordinates to give an étale map from V to affine space of dimension m+d over k. The old coordinates occur in the first m positions. Their sections are the pullbacks from W, which are also the pullbacks from U by compatibility with restriction.

If an ideal sheaf restricts to the unit ideal on U, its section ideal on W is the unit ideal and remains so after extension to V. If it is the chart ideal of a set S on U, on W its section ideal is generated by the restricted coordinate sections indexed by S. Extension to V takes these generators to the corresponding first-block coordinates. On the affine open V this ideal of sections determines the restricted ideal sheaf, which is exactly the new chart ideal of the image of S.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_etale_mvPolynomialHom_castAdd_coo:
Write A for the ring of sections on W and B for the ring of sections on V. The chart on W gives a formally étale map from the polynomial ring over k in m variables to A. Adjoining the d relative variables on both sides is a base change, so the resulting map from the polynomial ring in all m+d variables to the polynomial ring over A in d variables is formally étale. The relative chart on V gives a formally étale evaluation map from that last ring to B. Hence the composite is formally étale.

Under this composite a scalar from k first becomes the corresponding scalar section on W and then its pullback on V. An old variable first becomes the corresponding coordinate section on W and then its pullback. These identifications show that the composite is compatible with the k-algebra structure on B. The ring B is of finite type over k by smoothness, so it is also of finite type over the polynomial source. That source is Noetherian, making the composite finitely presented and therefore étale. Reindex the variables by putting the old block first and the relative block last. This polynomial-ring isomorphism preserves both the scalar formula and the required old-coordinate formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.finiteType_sectionsAlgebra_of_isAffineOp: The composite Y → X → Spec k is smooth because both maps are smooth. On the affine open V, its structure algebra of sections is therefore of finite type over k.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_comap: A point in the support of the pulled-back centre maps into the support of Z. At that image choose a common chart for Z and E, and extend the chart near the chosen point of Y by adding the relative coordinates. Transport the assignment for the divisors into the first coordinate block. The transported chart satisfies the divisor conditions by the preceding verification. The centre was cut out by S in the original chart, so its pullback is cut out by the image of S in that same first block. This gives the required common chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_affineOpen_eq_top_of_restrictIdeal: The global ideal of the restriction to V is the extension of the section ideal on V along the canonical section-ring isomorphism. By hypothesis this extension is the whole ring. Applying the inverse ring isomorphism gives the whole original section ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_top_of_map_eq_top_of_leftInvers: Extend the image ideal along g. This is I because the composite of the two ring maps is the identity. It is also the unit ideal, since extension takes the unit ideal of B to the unit ideal of A.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_comap: Each member of the pulled-back list comes from a member of E, so its smoothness follows from the pulled-back divisor result. At an arbitrary y in Y, take the chart for E at the image of y and extend it to a chart near y. Transport the coordinate assignment by including the old index set into the first block. The preceding verification gives distinctness and both ideal conditions, establishing the local chart requirement at y.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_comap_sin: Apply the list pullback theorem to the list with sole entry H. Its pulled-back list has sole entry equal to the pullback of H.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_comap_of_mem_inStrictNor: Choose an occurrence of D in the list E. At each point y of Y, take a strict normal crossing chart at its image in X and extend it to a chart near y. In the original chart the occurrence of D either has unit restriction or is cut out by one coordinate. In the new chart its pullback has unit restriction in the first case and is cut out by the corresponding first-block coordinate in the second. The local coordinate criterion therefore gives a smooth divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_eq_top_of_ideal_eq_top: The ideal of the restricted sheaf on the affine scheme V is the extension of the section ideal on V along the canonical map to its global section ring. That section ideal is the unit ideal, whose extension is again the unit ideal. An ideal sheaf on an affine scheme is determined by its global ideal, so the restricted sheaf is the unit ideal sheaf.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictNormalCrossings_chart_conditions_c:
The list of pullbacks has the same positions as E. Leave each unassigned position unassigned, and send each assigned coordinate to its index in the first block of the larger chart. If two positions get the same new coordinate, injectivity of the inclusion of the first block gives the same original coordinate, and the old assignment gives equality of the positions.

An unassigned position had unit restriction on U, so its pullback has unit restriction on V by hypothesis. For an assigned position, apply the pullback formula for coordinate ideals to the singleton containing its original coordinate. Its image is the singleton containing the new coordinate, as required.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sumEquiv_castAdd_eq_inl: In the partition of the m+d indices into an initial block of size m and a final block of size d, the index coming from j in the first block corresponds to j in the first summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topIso_hom_inv_apply: The section-ring identification is an isomorphism. Applying its inverse to x and then applying the forward map returns x.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ι_appLE_self_top_eq_topIso_inv: Pullback of a section on V along its open inclusion regards the section as a global section of the open subscheme V. This is precisely the inverse of the canonical identification of those global sections with sections on V.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_index_map_of_filterNeTop_eq: Enumerate the positions of the nonunit entries of each list in increasing order. For each nonunit position i of E′, send it to the position of the same rank in this enumeration for E. The enumerations have the same length because the filtered lists are equal, and their entries at each rank carry equal ideals. Distinct nonunit positions of E′ have distinct ranks and hence distinct images. Define the map arbitrarily at all other positions, where the conclusion imposes no requirements.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filterNeTop_cons_of_ne_top: The first ideal passes the test for being different from the unit ideal. It is retained as the first entry, followed by the filtered tail.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filterNeTop_cons_top: The first ideal is the unit ideal and fails the filter. The result is the filtered tail.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.filterNeTop_nil: Filtering only retains entries of the original list. The empty list has none, so the filtered list is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_of_filterNe: Match the nonunit positions of E′ to equal entries of E by their order in the common filtered list. At each point of the support of Z, take the chart for Z and E and transport the divisor assignment through that match. The transport lemma gives the conditions for E′. The chart and the coordinate set cutting out Z are the original witnesses, so they still give the required ideal for Z.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPositionAt_of_filt: Choose the neighbourhood, chart, and assignment for E at x. Equality of the filtered lists gives the injective correspondence from nonunit positions of E′ to equal entries of E. Transport the assignment to E′ by this correspondence and assign no coordinates to whole-scheme unit entries. The transport lemma proves distinctness and both local ideal conditions in the same chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_of_filter: At each point, transfer the local chart from E to E′ by equality of the filtered lists. To check smoothness of each entry of E′, use the smooth-divisor result for the unit ideal. Any nonunit entry belongs to the filtered list of E′, hence to the filtered list of E and to E itself. Its smoothness follows from the hypothesis on E.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_top: At each point of the smooth scheme, choose an étale coordinate chart. The unit ideal restricts to the unit ideal on that neighbourhood, so the local coordinate criterion applies everywhere and yields a smooth divisor in the stated sense.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_filterNeTop: Take an occurrence of D in E. Since D differs from the unit ideal, the filter retains that occurrence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_of_mem_filterNeTop: Every occurrence retained by the filter comes from an occurrence in the original list, giving the asserted membership.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transportAssignment_injective_and_coordI:
Any position assigned a coordinate is nonunit, so it corresponds to an equal ideal at a valid index in E. If two positions receive the same coordinate, injectivity of the original assignment forces their matched indices to agree. Injectivity of the index correspondence then gives equality of the two positions.

A unit entry restricts to the unit ideal. For an unassigned nonunit entry, the matching entry of E is also unassigned and has unit restriction by the original chart. For an assigned entry, the matching entry of E has the same assigned coordinate and therefore restricts to the specified coordinate ideal. The corresponding ideals in E′ have the same restrictions because the entries are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transportAssignment_of_eq_top: The transport rule assigns no coordinate to an entry equal to the unit ideal. Apply that branch of the rule at the given index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transportAssignment_of_ne_top: At a position whose entry is different from the unit ideal, the transport rule uses the original assignment at the matched index. This gives the stated value.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_comp_subschemeι_eq_subschemeι_com: The fibre product of Y with the closed subscheme defined by Z over X is closed in Y with ideal the pullback of Z. The closed subscheme defined by that pulled-back ideal therefore factors through the fibre product over Y. Composing this factorization with the projection to the original closed subscheme gives the required map. The pullback square gives the equality of composites into X.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pow_mul_mem_of_ideal_basicOpen_eq: Restriction to the basic open of f localizes the section ring by inverting f. The image of s belongs to the extension of A's ideal, which equals the extension of B's ideal by the hypothesis on the basic open. Membership in the localized ideal gives a power of f whose product with s belongs to B's ideal, by clearing denominators.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_of_comp_subschemeι_eq_of_iso_pullba: Under the given isomorphism to the fibre product, the second projection gives a map with the same composite into X as q. The inclusion of the original closed subscheme is a monomorphism, so q equals this transported projection. The projection is the base change of the flat map g. Its composite with the isomorphism is flat.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_subschemeMapOfComap: The closed subscheme of the pulled-back ideal is canonically isomorphic to the fibre product over X. Its map to the original closed subscheme satisfies the required factorization identity. Thus it is the transported fibre-product projection, which is flat by base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.generalizing_subschemeMapOfComap: The map of the pulled-back closed subscheme to the original one is flat. The going-down property of a flat morphism lifts the given generization of the image of y to a generization of y, giving the required point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafData_eq_of_forall_restrictIdea: Fix an affine open W. At each point of W, intersect its neighbourhood of equality with W and choose a basic open of W about the point contained in that intersection. The restrictions of the ideal sheaves still agree there, so their section ideals on this basic open agree. These opens cover W. The basic-open comparison gives an inclusion of the section ideals on W in each direction, and hence equality. Equality on every affine open identifies the sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_of_comap_opensι_eq: View V as an affine scheme. Its global ideals for the restricted sheaves are obtained from the original section ideals over V by the canonical section-ring isomorphism. The restricted sheaves agree, so these global ideals agree. Transport them back along the inverse ring isomorphism to identify the original section ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_le_of_basicOpen_cover: Fix s in the section ideal of A. For each section f in the covering family, a power of f times s belongs to the section ideal of B by the localization criterion. Hence the ideal of elements multiplying s into B contains a power of each f. A prime containing that ideal would then contain every covering section. Since those sections generate the unit ideal, no such prime exists. The multiplying ideal is the whole ring, so s belongs to B.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_connectedComponent_of_specializes: Since y specializes to z, the point z lies in the closure of the singleton containing y. This closure is connected and contains y, so both points lie in the connected component of y. That component is the same as the connected component of x because y belongs to it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_of_subschemeMapOfComap_apply_mem: The continuous map on closed subschemes sends the connected component of y into the connected component of its image. The latter lies over A by the assumption that the image belongs to W. The commuting square shows that every point of the component of y therefore lies over the inverse image of A. By the definition of W′ this puts y in W′.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.openSubschemeKer_comap:
Check the two ideal sheaves on a neighbourhood of each point y of Y. If the image of y belongs to the image of W, choose an open U around it whose inverse image in the original closed subscheme lies in W. The inverse image of U in the pulled-back closed subscheme lies in W′ by the forward component implication. On these neighbourhoods the kernels of the two open pieces agree with the kernels of the respective full closed subschemes. Those kernels agree by pullback and restriction.

If the image of y is outside the image of W, choose an open U around it disjoint from that image, using that W is closed in the closed subscheme. No point of W′ lies over U, since the reverse component implication would put its image in W. Both open-piece kernels thus restrict to the unit ideal on the corresponding neighbourhoods. In both cases the local kernels agree. Local equality gives the desired equality of ideal sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap_preimage_eq_comap_re: The inclusion of the inverse-image open followed by g equals the restricted map followed by the inclusion of U. Pullback of I along this common composite can therefore be computed by either restriction order, giving the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.span_eq_top_of_basicOpen_cover: Identify the affine open W with the spectrum of its section ring. If the chosen sections generated a proper ideal, some maximal ideal would contain them all. Its point would lie outside every one of their basic opens, contradicting the cover. Hence their span is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeMapOfComap_apply_mem_of_mem:
Take the generic point of the irreducible connected component of the image of y in the original closed subscheme. It is a generization of that image. Flatness lifts it to a generization y′ of y, which belongs to the same connected component as y. The definition of W′ now puts the image of y′ in A after composing to X. By the commuting square this is the image in X of the chosen generic point.

Every point of the original component is a specialization of that generic point. The map to X preserves specialization, and A is closed, so the image of the whole component lies in A. This is the condition for the image of y to belong to W.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeMapOfComap_base: Apply the commuting-square identity for the scheme morphisms to the underlying point y. Functoriality of the underlying point map gives the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeMapOfComap_comp: The chosen map from the pulled-back closed subscheme is the witness in the preceding factorization. It satisfies the commuting-square identity by that construction.

Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLi.Formalism.VW.critLine:
A zero strictly to the right of the critical line contradicts the assumed nonvanishing at once. Suppose it lies strictly to the left. The gamma factor at s is nonzero, so the completed L-function also vanishes there. The inverse character is primitive because inversion preserves its conductor. Its functional equation now gives a zero of the completed L-function at 1 − s.

Dividing by the gamma factor transfers that zero to the ordinary L-function of the inverse character. The point 1 − s has real part greater than 1/2 and is distinct from 1, so this again contradicts the assumed nonvanishing. The remaining possibility is Re(s) = 1/2.
Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLi.Formalism.VW.gammaFactor_ne_zero: For an even character the factor is Γℝ(s), and for an odd character it is Γℝ(s + 1). Both arguments have positive real part. The real gamma factor is nonzero in that half-plane.
Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLi.Formalism.VW.rh_of_every: Take the trivial character of modulus 1, whose L-function equals the zeta function. The assumed nonvanishing for all characters therefore excludes zeta zeros with real part greater than 1/2 away from 1. The reduction for zeros of the zeta function now gives the Riemann Hypothesis.

Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/RhOfRi.Formalism.VW.rh_of_right:
Let s be a nontrivial zero distinct from 1. The value of zeta at 0 also excludes s = 0. The assumed nonvanishing rules out Re(s) > 1/2. If Re(s) < 1/2, set t = 1 − s. Then Re(t) > 1/2 and t is distinct from 1, so ζ(t) is nonzero. The functional equation expresses ζ(s) as the product of ζ(t), Γ(t), cos(πt/2), and 2(2π)^(−t). The gamma and power factors are nonzero.

If the cosine vanished, t would equal 2k + 1 for an integer k, giving s = −2k. A negative k contradicts Re(s) < 1/2. The value k = 0 gives s = 0, and a positive k gives an excluded trivial zero. Thus the cosine factor is also nonzero. This contradicts ζ(s) = 0, so Re(s) = 1/2.

Formalism/LocalToGlobal/GroupLattices/Ti.FullTiedNoG.toFull_base: Completing the datum copies the underlying tied data from X and adds g. Its base projection is therefore the original base of X.
Formalism/LocalToGlobal/GroupLattices/Ti.FullTiedNoG.toFull_g: Completing the datum sets the G-data to g. The G-data are therefore the supplied g.
Formalism/LocalToGlobal/GroupLattices/Ti.adSet: The change of datum replaces the assigned G-data and its dimension certificate. The adjacency conditions use the original lattice and step data, the Hermitian columns, and the data at T. The change of datum copies the Hermitian columns and the data at T field by field. Consequently the upward, downward, and dilation conditions at level zero and at positive levels are identical to the six supplied conditions in h. Use those six fields for the new adjacency structure.
Formalism/LocalToGlobal/GroupLattices/Ti.full_setting_level_zero: The adjusted tied datum is built by applying the Hermitian change of datum to the original base. That change copies the level-zero field, so the completed datum has the original level-zero data.
Formalism/LocalToGlobal/GroupLattices/Ti.hermitian_setting_level_zero: The change of datum copies the tied Hermitian fields from H. In particular, its level-zero Hermitian data are those of H.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.exists_constant_exponent_inequalities:
Take C = 100000. Put G = w+S+η and z = G+1, so b ≥ 100000(j+1)z ≥ 200000z. This gives max(G,1) < b ≤ min(b₀,b₁) and η < b. Hence b₀ ≤ b+η < 2b ≤ 2b₁, which gives both comparisons with ℓb₁ because ℓ ≥ 11.

For the final bound use g = max(G,1) ≤ z and H = b+η+S ≤ b+G in the preceding bounds for the two exponents. The definition a₀ = 2σ + rr + 2g·ell and ell ≤ 3j+1 then with σ denoting the sigma exponent give a₀ < 0.242b + (6j+20000)z by collecting the coefficients. For j ≥ 1, 6j+20000 ≤ 11000(j+1), so the second term is at most 0.11b. Thus a₀ < b/2 ≤ b₁/2.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.log_nat_le: At h = 0 the real logarithm is zero by convention. For h > 0, split log h as log(h/1000) + log 1000. Apply log t ≤ t−1 to both terms and add the bounds.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.mpar_le: The integer quotient in Mpar is bounded by the real quotient (h+2g)/(ℓ−1). Since ℓ−1 ≥ 10 and the numerator is nonnegative, replace the denominator by 10. Adding 1 gives the claim.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.rr_le: For the two rational terms use ℓ ≥ 11 and (ℓ−1)^(j+1) ≥ 10². Since log ℓ ≥ 1 and log h ≥ 0 for natural h under the real logarithm convention, log base ℓ of h is at most log h. Use the upper bound for the logarithm of a natural number and substitute the three bounds into the assumption on rr.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.sig_lt: The power ℓ^(j−1) is at least 1, so the Mpar term after division by that power is bounded by Mpar itself. For ℓ ≥ 11, the bound ℓ/(ℓ−1)² ≤ 11/100 follows after clearing denominators from (ℓ−11)(11ℓ−1) ≥ 0. Substitute the bound on Mpar, then use that the ceiling of a nonnegative real is strictly less than that real plus 1. The 1 already in the argument of the ceiling makes the total rounding allowance 2.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.arc_exponential_identity: Because G ≥ 0 and j′ ≤ ell, we have j′G ≤ ell·G. If the maximum is 2σ+2j′G+1, bound it by 2σ+2ell·G+1 and add the prefactor. If the maximum is r+κ, the left side becomes 2r+4σ+2κ. The right side is larger by the nonnegative quantity 2σ+2ell·G+1.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.eta_determinant_comparison: Apply the determinant comparison input with the supplied ring action and element Θ. Its remaining premise is the product congruence for an arbitrary tuple of elements of R′ and a test point. View each tuple entry as a matrix-valued function over the fraction field. The hypothesis on R′ gives the action compatibility for each of these functions, so the product congruence input applies and supplies the premise.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.mem_span_of_C_pow_mul:
Write C(aᵛ)g = p C(aᵗ) + qXᵇ using membership in the two-generator ideal. For every degree n < b, the last term has coefficient zero. Comparing degree-n coefficients therefore gives aᵛgₙ = aᵗpₙ. Since a is nonzero and v ≤ t, cancel aᵛ to obtain gₙ = a^(t−v)pₙ.

Thus every coefficient of g − p C(a^(t−v)) below degree b vanishes. This difference is divisible by Xᵇ, so g is a linear combination of C(a^(t−v)) and Xᵇ.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.mem_span_of_X_pow_mul:
Write X^ηg = F C(a) + G X^(b+η), where C(a) is the constant series a. If a = 0, the first term vanishes. Cancel X^η, which is nonzero in the power series domain, to obtain g = G X^b.

For a ≠ 0, rearrange to get F C(a) = X^η(g − G X^b). Its coefficients of degree below η vanish. Each is a times the corresponding coefficient of F, so that coefficient of F vanishes in the domain. Thus F = X^ηF′. Substitute this into the original equality and cancel X^η to obtain g = F′ C(a) + G X^b, which proves the desired ideal membership.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.column_assembly_bound: Use the chain length inequality to bound the length by the sum of layer lengths and the terminal length. For i in gen, the chosen generators and Fᵢ₊₁ span Fᵢ, so the quotient length bound for a finite spanning set applies with Bc = Fᵢ₊₁ and I = Fᵢ₊₁+P. This gives coefficient me′ in units of the length of O/(ℓ). For each other i, the assumed bound gives coefficient L. There are |gen| indices of the first kind and k−|gen| of the second because gen is contained in the index range. Add the layer estimates. Finally the bound for a submodule generated by a basis gives coefficient rank(M)·e for the terminal length. Factoring out the common length proves the formula.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.len_bound: Since Bc is contained in I, its image is zero in Z/(Z∩I). The equality Z = span(s)+Bc then says the classes of s generate the quotient. They are killed by a^e, and therefore give a surjection from |s| copies of O/(a^e). Each copy has length at most e times the length of O/(a). Use |s| ≤ g to finish.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.len_chain: At k = 0 the initial term is the quotient M/P, since F₀ is the full module. In the induction step apply the two-step length equality to Fₖ₊₁ ≤ Fₖ. It rewrites the old terminal length as the next layer length plus the next terminal length. Insert that equality into the bound for k and append the new summand.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.len_two_step: Include B/(B∩P) into A/(A∩P) and then quotient A by A∩(B+P). The inclusion is injective because an element of B represents zero in A/(A∩P) exactly when it is in P. The second map is onto. Its kernel consists of classes of a = b+p, with b in B and p in P. These are precisely the image of the first map, since a and b have the same class. Add lengths in the resulting short exact sequence.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.sub_gen: Take a basis of F over the principal ideal domain and view its vectors in M. They form a finite spanning set of size at most the rank of F, which is at most the rank of M. Apply the quotient length bound for a finite spanning set with Bc = 0, I = P, and g equal to the rank of M, using the hypothesis that a^e kills the classes of F modulo P.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.chain_len_add: Use the maps Y/X → Z/X → Z/Y induced by inclusion and quotient. The inclusion is injective because a representative from Y becomes zero exactly when it lies in X. The quotient map is surjective because the same representative in Z can be used in either quotient. Its kernel consists of classes represented by elements of Y, precisely the image of the inclusion. Length additivity for this short exact sequence gives the equality.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.chain_len_le_of_le_sup: Use the map from A/(A∩X) to Z/(Z∩X) induced by inclusion. Given a representative z in Z, write z = a+x with a in A and x in X, using Z ≤ A+X. The class of z is the image of the class of a. The map is surjective, so the target has length at most the source.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.chain_len_le_top: The map A/(A∩P) → M/P sends the class of a to its class in M/P. Every m in M can be written as a+p by the assumption M = A+P, so this map is surjective. Apply the length inequality for a surjection.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.column_chain_bound:
Induct on k. At k = 0 the sum is empty, and the terminal quotient represents the whole quotient since F₀ is the full module. For the induction step write U = Fₖ, V = Fₖ₊₁, X = P∩U, and Y = (V+P)∩U. Length additivity decomposes the old terminal term length(U/X) into length(Y/X) and length(U/Y). The latter is the new summand.

Since V ≤ U, the modular law gives Y = V+(P∩U). The map V/(V∩P) → Y/X is surjective by this equality, so length(Y/X) is bounded by the new terminal term. Substitute the two bounds into the induction hypothesis and append the new summand.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.comap_subtype_inf_of_le: An element of A already lies in C by the inclusion A ≤ C. Membership in B∩C on restricting to A is therefore equivalent to membership in B, giving equality of the two restricted submodules.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.comap_subtype_span_sup_eq_span_range_sup: Write A for the ambient span of s, which lies in Z. After mapping the two submodules into the ambient module via the inclusion of Z, the left side is (A+J) ∩ Z. The internal generators map to exactly the elements of s, so the right side maps to A+(J∩Z). These images agree by the modular law, since A ≤ Z. Injectivity of the inclusion gives equality of the submodules in Z.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.length_quotient_le_of_two_step:
Inside Z/(I∩Z), let N be the image of the span of s₀. The restriction identity for spans shows that N is generated by the classes of s₀. They are killed by ℓ^e′, so the length of N is at most g₀e′ times the length of O/(ℓ). Indeed, a module generated by g₀ such classes is a quotient of g₀ copies of O/(ℓ^e′), and each copy has length at most e′ times the length of O/(ℓ).

The quotient by N is Z modulo the restriction of span(s₀)+I. The classes of s generate this quotient because span(s)+I = Z, and these classes are killed by ℓ^e. The same estimate gives the bound with ge. Add both estimates along the exact sequence for N.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.mem_cl: For the false orientation, membership in the window requires h−η ≤ u ≤ h−1. The strict inequality u < h−η excludes u from the window. Since u belongs to U, it belongs to the filtered complement for the false orientation.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.t3: The element u lies in the false-orientation complement by the preceding window comparison. Apply residue avoidance to u and k with the given lower and upper bounds on k. In this orientation the residue being tested is h−u.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.tele: Induct on the interval length k. At length zero the interval is empty and both sides equal M(a). For length k+1, add the endpoint a+k to the previous interval. The local relation at that endpoint gives f(a+k) + M(a+k+1) = g(a+k) + M(a+k), with arguments read modulo ℓ. Use this identity to move the new boundary term back to a+k, then apply the induction hypothesis to the old interval.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.chain_of_step: Take the chain of length one with cuts a and b. Its only step is the supplied step from a to b.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.chain_trans: Concatenate the cut sequences, identifying the last cut of the first chain with the first cut of the second chain at b. Use the first chain's indices through its endpoint and subtract its length from each later index. Each adjacent pair lies in one of the original chains, including the pair that starts at b. Hence every pair is a valid step, and the endpoints are a and d.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.cluster_chain:
Induct on a natural bound for the distance B−a. Let f be the first marked point after a, which exists at or before B. The empty starting interval forces f > a+j. Set s = f−1−a. If the j places after f are empty, take e = f. Otherwise choose a marked g within that window and take e = g. The pair lemma gives an empty j-window after g and excludes marks strictly between f and g. Also g ≤ B, since otherwise B would either lie strictly between f and g or, if B = f, have a marked point in its own empty window.

In either case the tail (a+s,e] contains at most two marks, namely f and possibly g, and has length at most j+1. Apply fill to reach e. If e = B this is the desired chain. Otherwise e has an empty starting window and B−e is strictly smaller than B−a. Apply induction and concatenate.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.fill:
Use strong induction on the length s of the initial empty interval. If s < 2j, go directly from a to e. The length is at least j and at most s+j+1 ≤ 3j. The first j places are empty, and every marked point up to e lies after a+s. There are at most two such points by the tail assumption, so the direct step is valid.

If s ≥ 2j, first take a step of length j through the empty interval. From a+j, the remaining empty interval has length s−j ≥ j and still ends at a+s, so the tail assumptions are unchanged. The induction hypothesis gives a chain for this shorter interval. Concatenate the initial step and that chain.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.main:
If there are no marked points, take a = 0 and use fill on the empty interval of length n, with no tail. Otherwise start with a marked point t₀. If the next j places are empty, take t = t₀. If there is a mark g among them, take t = g, whose next j places are empty by the pair lemma.

Periodicity makes B = t+n a marked point and transfers the empty window after t to the window after B. Since n ≥ j+1 and j ≥ 1, the cut-chain lemma applies from t to B with distance bound n. This gives a chain spanning one period.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.pair:
At the marked point g, the cluster condition must take its second form because f is a marked predecessor within distance j. The unique permitted predecessor in the stated range is therefore f itself. All points strictly between f and g are excluded.

If there were a marked point h in (g,g+j], apply the same condition at h. The permitted predecessor would have to be g, at distance h−g. But f would be a second marked predecessor at distance (h−g)+(g−f), which is at most (h−g)+j. This violates the exclusion range at h. Hence the whole interval (g,g+j] is empty.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.expBound_statement:
Put H = h+η, d = ℓ−1, and L = lam(ℓ,H). Insert the upper bounds on s₁, e₂, and both occurrences of E. Bound b by H and the integer quotient in sig by h/d ≤ H/d. The terms involving a now sum to 8a/d. By the assumption on a and the definition of aR, this contributes at most 8H(2ℓ−1)/d³ + (32+8L)/d.

Collect the H terms to obtain H·[8(2ℓ−1)/d³ + 8/d² + 1/(ℓd)]. The coefficient bound gives at most 32H/ℓ². The remaining terms are 10η/d, (3+3/d)S, and 9L+10+(34+8L)/d. Since d ≥ 10, the S coefficient is at most 4. Since L ≥ 1, the last group is at most 24L. These are the required terms.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.hcoef_le: Bound the three terms by (41/2)/x², 10/x², and (11/10)/x², respectively. For the first two, clear the positive denominators and put t = x−11 ≥ 0. The differences become (9/2)t³+95t²+518t+172 and 2t²+24t+32. For the third, the cleared inequality is 10x ≤ 11(x−1). Adding the three bounds gives 31.6/x² ≤ 32/x².
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.lam_ge_one: If H = 0, log base ℓ of 2H is zero by the real logarithm convention. If H is positive, then 2H ≥ 1, so this logarithm is nonnegative since ℓ > 1. In either case adding 1 gives at least 1.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.first_sigma_valuation_bound:
Bound the sum on the union by the two interval sums with zero removed. On the first interval, reflect the negative integers and keep the positive ones. Valuation depends only on absolute value, so the two pieces are bounded by the factorial valuations at η−1 and η+a, using natural subtraction for η−1.

The second interval lies entirely below zero because b ≥ 2a+η+1. Reflection gives the interval from m+1 through m+a+S, where m = b−a−1. Its valuation sum is vℓ((m+a+S)!)−vℓ(m!). The binomial coefficient bound gives at most vℓ((a+S)!) + logℓ(m+a+S), with the integer logarithm in this expression.

Apply vℓ(N!) ≤ N/(ℓ−1) to the three factorial terms. Their numerator is at most 2a+2η+S. The integer logarithm is bounded by lam(ℓ,h+η), since m+a+S ≤ b+S ≤ h and the nonzero argument case follows by taking logs of ℓ^logℓ(N) ≤ N. For a zero argument the integer logarithm is zero. Finally lam(ℓ,h+η) is nonnegative, so increasing the logarithmic allowance to twice this quantity gives the stated bound.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.padicValNat_factorial_add_le_add_log: Factor (m+L)! as the product of m!, L!, and the binomial coefficient choosing L from m+L. These factors are positive, so their valuations add. The valuation of the binomial coefficient is at most the integer logarithm of m+L by the prime-factorization bound for binomial coefficients. Add this bound to the other two valuations.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.sub_one_mul_padicValNat_factorial_le': Use the factorial valuation formula (ℓ−1)vℓ(N!) = N − sℓ(N), where sℓ is the base-ℓ digit sum. Its nonnegativity gives the desired bound.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.sum_Icc_one_padicValNat_eq_factorial: Take m = 0 in the interval-factorial formula. The initial factorial is 0! = 1 with valuation zero, leaving the valuation of L! as the sum from 1 to L.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.sum_Icc_padicValNat_add_factorial_eq: At L = 0 the interval is empty. To increase L by one, add its new upper endpoint m+L+1 to the valuation sum. At the same time the factorial is multiplied by m+L+1. Valuations add under multiplication of these positive integers, so the induction identity is preserved.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.sum_erase_union_le: Removing zero from the union gives the union of the two sets with zero removed.
